title.raw: 卷66 李崇 崔亮 Volume 66: Li Chong, Cui Liang

sentences.zh: 李崇 崔亮

translations.literal: Li Chong, Cui Liang
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong and Cui Liang

sentences.zh: 李崇，字繼長，小名繼伯，頓丘人也，文成元皇后第二兄誕之子。

translations.literal: Li Chong, courtesy name Jichang, childhood name Jibo, was a man of Dunqiu, the son of Dan, second elder brother of Empress Yuan of Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, styled Jichang and known in youth as Jibo, was a native of Dunqiu and the son of Dan, younger brother of Empress Yuan, consort of Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 年十四，召拜主文中散，襲爵陳留公，鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was summoned and appointed Chief Clerk for Literary Affairs, inherited the title Duke of Chenliu, and was made General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was called to court as Chief Clerk for Literary Affairs, succeeded to the dukedom of Chenliu, and was appointed General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，為大使巡察冀州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he served as grand envoy inspecting Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Gaozu he was sent as a grand inspector to Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官行梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he acted as Governor of Liang Province in his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dispatched to Liang Province, serving concurrently in his present post.

sentences.zh: 時巴氐擾動，詔崇以本將軍為荊州刺史，鎮上洛，敕發陝秦二州兵送崇至治。

translations.literal: At that time the Ba and Di were in turmoil; an edict appointed Chong, with his present rank of general, Governor of Jing Province to garrison Shangluo, and ordered troops from Shaan and Qin Provinces to escort Chong to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ba and Di peoples rose in unrest, the emperor ordered Chong, retaining his general's rank, to govern Jing Province from Shangluo and commanded forces from Shaan and Qin to convey him to his post.

sentences.zh: 崇辭曰：「邊人失和，本怨刺史，奉詔代之，自然易帖。

translations.literal: Chong declined, saying: "The border people have lost harmony; their grievance is fundamentally against the governor. If I go to replace him by imperial order, they will naturally be easy to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Chong respectfully objected: "The frontier population is unsettled because they resent their governor. Once I arrive under imperial appointment to take his place, they should readily submit.

sentences.zh: 但須一宣詔旨而已，不勞發兵自防，使懷懼也。」

translations.literal: One need only proclaim the edict; there is no need to mobilize troops for self-defense and thereby inspire fear."
translations.idiomatic: All that is required is to announce the imperial decree—there is no need to march an army for my protection and frighten them further."

sentences.zh: 高祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 乃輕將數十騎馳到上洛，宣詔綏慰，當即帖然。

translations.literal: Then with only a few dozen mounted followers he galloped to Shangluo, proclaimed the edict, and soothed the people; at once all was calm.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode swiftly to Shangluo with only a few dozen horsemen, issued the edict, and reassured the people—and peace was restored immediately.

sentences.zh: 尋勒邊戍，掠得蕭賾人者，悉令還之。

translations.literal: Before long he ordered the frontier garrisons: any captives taken from Xiao Ze's domain were to be returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon instructed the border posts that any subjects seized from the domain of Xiao Ze must be sent home.

sentences.zh: 南人感德，仍送荊州之口二百許人。

translations.literal: The southerners, moved by his virtue, in turn sent back some two hundred people who had been held in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Touched by his fairness, the southerners themselves returned roughly two hundred captives who had been held in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 兩境交和，無復烽燧之警。

translations.literal: The two frontiers were at peace, and there were no longer alarms from beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony prevailed along both borders, and beacon warnings ceased.

sentences.zh: 在治四年，甚有稱績。

translations.literal: During four years in office he earned considerable praise for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In four years of administration his record won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 召還京師，賞賜隆厚。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he received lavish gifts and honors.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: With his present rank of general he was appointed Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his general's title, he was made governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 兗土舊多劫盜，崇乃村置一樓，樓懸一鼓，盜發之處，雙槌亂擊。

translations.literal: Yan territory had long been plagued by bandits; Chong therefore placed a tower in each village, hung a drum from it, and wherever robbers struck both mallets were beaten wildly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province had long suffered from banditry, so Chong erected a watchtower in every village, suspended a drum from each, and whenever thieves appeared the drums were beaten with both mallets at once.

sentences.zh: 四面諸村始聞者撾鼓一通，次復聞者以二為節，次後聞者以三為節，各擊數千槌。

translations.literal: Of the surrounding villages, those who first heard the alarm struck once; those who heard next used two beats as their signal; those who heard afterward used three; each village beat thousands of strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The nearest village sounded one roll; the next relay beat twice; those farther out answered with three beats—each settlement pounding its drum thousands of times.

sentences.zh: 諸村聞鼓，皆守要路，是以盜發俄頃之間，聲布百里之內。

translations.literal: When the villages heard the drums they all guarded the key roads, so that within moments of a robbery the alarm spread a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Every village that heard the drums blocked the vital routes, and within moments news of a theft carried a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 其中險要，悉有伏人，盜竊始發，便爾擒送。

translations.literal: At every strategic point men lay in ambush; as soon as thieves appeared they were seized and delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushes waited at every choke point, and robbers were captured the moment they struck.

sentences.zh: 諸州置樓懸鼓，自崇始也。

translations.literal: The practice of setting towers and hanging drums in the provinces began with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial watchtowers and alarm drums were first instituted by Chong.

sentences.zh: 後例降為侯，改授安東將軍。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent his noble rank was reduced to marquis and he was reassigned as General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was lowered by precedent to marquis, and he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 東駕南征，驃騎大將軍、咸陽王禧都督左翼諸軍事，詔崇以本官副焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched south on campaign, General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Xianyang, Xi, commanded the left wing; an edict appointed Chong as his deputy in his existing office.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern expedition, Prince Xi of Xianyang, General of Agile Cavalry, directed the left wing, and Chong was ordered to serve as his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 徐州降人郭陸聚黨作逆，人多應之，搔擾南北。

translations.literal: Guo Lu of Xuzhou, a surrendered man, gathered a faction and rebelled; many joined him, harassing north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Lu, a defector from Xuzhou, raised a rebel band that drew widespread support and ravaged both sides of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 崇遣高平人卜冀州詐稱犯罪，逃亡歸陸。

translations.literal: Chong sent Bu Jizhou of Gaoping, who feigned guilt and fled to join Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong dispatched Bu Jizhou of Gaoping, who pretended to be a fugitive criminal and sought refuge with Lu.

sentences.zh: 陸納之，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Lu took him in and made him chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Lu welcomed him and appointed him his chief adviser.

sentences.zh: 數月，冀州斬陸送之，賊徒潰散。

translations.literal: After several months Jizhou beheaded Lu and sent the head; the band dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Jizhou killed Lu and delivered his head, and the rebels collapsed.

sentences.zh: 入為河南尹。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Henan Intendancy.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Director of the Henan Intendancy.

sentences.zh: 後車駕南討漢陽，崇行梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned south against Hanyang, Chong acted as Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the court later marched south against Hanyang, Chong again governed Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 氐楊靈珍遣弟婆羅與子雙領步騎萬餘，襲破武興，與蕭鸞相結。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Yang Lingzhen sent his younger brother Poluo and his son Shuang at the head of more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to storm and seize Wuxing, allying with Xiao Luan.
translations.idiomatic: The Di leader Yang Lingzhen sent his brother Poluo and his son Shuang with over ten thousand foot and horse to overrun Wuxing and enter an alliance with Xiao Luan.

sentences.zh: 詔崇為使持節、都督隴右諸軍事，率眾數萬討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Chong Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander of All Military Affairs in Longyou, leading tens of thousands to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was commissioned with the staff of authority to command all forces in Longyou and led tens of thousands against them.

sentences.zh: 崇槎山分進，出其不意，表裏以襲。

translations.literal: Chong advanced by separate routes over mountain paths, taking them unawares and striking from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Chong divided his army to march over mountain trails, catching the enemy off guard and attacking from both front and rear.

sentences.zh: 羣氐皆棄靈珍散歸，靈珍眾減太半。

translations.literal: The Di clans all abandoned Lingzhen and scattered homeward; Lingzhen's forces were more than halved.
translations.idiomatic: The Di tribes deserted Lingzhen and fled to their homes, and his army shrank by more than half.

sentences.zh: 崇進據赤土，靈珍又遣從弟建率五千人屯龍門，躬率精勇一萬據鷲硤。

translations.literal: Chong advanced and occupied Chitu; Lingzhen again sent his cousin Jian with five thousand men to hold Longmen while he personally led ten thousand picked warriors to hold Jiuxia.
translations.idiomatic: Chong pressed forward to Chitu; Lingzhen sent his cousin Jian with five thousand men to guard Longmen while he himself held Jiuxia Pass with ten thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 龍門之北數十里中伐樹塞路，鷲硤之口積大木，聚礌石，臨崖下之，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: For several tens of li north of Longmen they felled trees to block the road; at the mouth of Jiuxia they piled great logs and gathered boulders to roll down the cliffs and repel the government army.
translations.idiomatic: For miles north of Longmen they cut trees to bar the road; at Jiuxia they heaped logs and stones to hurl from the cliffs against the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 崇乃命統軍慕容拒率眾五千，從他路夜襲龍門，破之。

translations.literal: Chong then ordered the commander Murong Ju to lead five thousand men by another route to raid Longmen by night and break it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong ordered Commander Murong Ju to take five thousand men by a side path and storm Longmen by night, which fell.

sentences.zh: 崇乃自攻靈珍，靈珍連戰敗走，俘其妻子。

translations.literal: Chong then personally attacked Lingzhen; Lingzhen was repeatedly defeated and fled, and his wife and children were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then assailed Lingzhen in person; defeated again and again, Lingzhen fled, and his family was taken.

sentences.zh: 崇多設疑兵，襲克武興。

translations.literal: Chong set up many feints and by surprise recaptured Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Deploying numerous decoys, he retook Wuxing by surprise.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞梁州刺史陰廣宗遣參軍鄭猷、王思考率眾援靈珍。

translations.literal: Yin Guangzong, Governor of Liang Province under Xiao Luan, sent the staff officers Zheng You and Wang Sikao leading troops to aid Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guangzong, Liang governor for Xiao Luan, sent the officers Zheng You and Wang Sikao with reinforcements for Lingzhen.

sentences.zh: 崇大破之，并斬婆羅首，殺千餘人，俘獲猷等，靈珍走奔漢中。

translations.literal: Chong routed them utterly, beheaded Poluo, killed more than a thousand, captured You and the others, and Lingzhen fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chong crushed them, took Poluo's head, slew over a thousand men, captured You and his companions, and drove Lingzhen to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 高祖在南陽，覽表大悅，曰：「使朕無西顧之憂者，李崇之功也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, at Nanyang, read the report with great delight and said: "The one who frees Us from worry over the west is Li Chong's achievement."
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyang the emperor read the dispatch with delight and declared, "Li Chong is the man who lifts from Us all anxiety about the western frontier."

sentences.zh: 以崇為都督梁秦二州諸軍事、本將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong was made Commander of All Military Affairs in Liang and Qin Provinces, retaining his general's rank as Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was appointed commander of all forces in Liang and Qin, remaining general and governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 高祖手詔曰：「今仇、隴克清，鎮捍以德，文人威惠既宣，[1]實允遠寄，故敕授梁州，用寧邊服。

translations.literal: The emperor's handwritten edict said: "Now Qiu and Long are cleared; the frontier is to be held by virtue. Your civil and martial authority is already proclaimed—[1] this truly fulfills the far-reaching trust placed in you; therefore We appoint you to Liang Province to settle the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand: "With Qiu and Long now pacified, the border must be secured through moral sway. Your combined literary and martial prestige has been shown abroad—[1] you have indeed earned this distant commission; We therefore grant you Liang Province to bring quiet to the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 便可善思經略，去其可除，安其可育，公私所患，悉令芟夷。」

translations.literal: Consider your strategy carefully: remove what should be removed, nurture what should be nurtured, and cut down every public and private evil."
translations.idiomatic: Plan wisely: uproot what must go, settle what can grow, and eliminate every affliction, public or private."

sentences.zh: 及靈珍偷據白水，崇擊破之，靈珍遠遁。

translations.literal: When Lingzhen secretly held Baishui, Chong defeated him and Lingzhen fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzhen seized Baishui, Chong drove him off and Lingzhen fled deep into the hills.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，徵為右衞將軍，兼七兵尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was summoned as General of the Right Guard and concurrently Minister of the Seventh Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Chong was recalled as General of the Right Guard and concurrent Minister of the Seventh Bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋加撫軍將軍，正尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army and full Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and full ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 轉左衞將軍、相州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard and Grand Assessor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as General of the Left Guard and Grand Assessor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 魯陽蠻柳北喜、魯北燕等聚眾反叛，諸蠻悉應之，圍逼湖陽。

translations.literal: The Luyang barbarians Liu Beixi and Lu Beiyan and others gathered forces in rebellion; all the tribes responded, besieging Huyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Luyang tribesmen Liu Beixi, Lu Beiyan, and others rose in arms; the barbarian clans joined them and pressed Huyang.

sentences.zh: 游擊將軍李暉先鎮此城，盡力捍禦，賊勢甚盛。

translations.literal: The Mobile Commander Li Hui was already defending the city with all his strength; the rebels' momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Commander Li Hui held the city with every effort, but the rebels' strength was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 詔以崇為使持節、都督征蠻諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chong Bearer of the Staff and Commander of All Military Affairs for the Campaign Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chong received the staff of authority and command of all forces assigned to suppress the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 蠻眾數萬，屯據形要，以拒官軍。

translations.literal: The barbarian host numbered tens of thousands, encamped at strategic points to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of tribesmen held the key terrain against the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 崇累戰破之，斬北燕等，徙萬餘戶於幽并諸州。

translations.literal: Chong defeated them in repeated battles, beheaded Beiyan and others, and relocated more than ten thousand households to You and Bing Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After a series of victories Chong killed Beiyan and his fellows and resettled more than ten thousand households in You and Bing.

sentences.zh: 世宗追賞平氐之功，封魏昌縣開國伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong rewarded him retroactively for pacifying the Di: he was enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded his earlier victory over the Di by creating him Baron of Weichang, fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 東荊州蠻樊安，聚眾於龍山，僭稱大號，蕭衍共為脣齒，遣兵應之。

translations.literal: In eastern Jing Province the barbarian Fan An gathered followers on Longshan, arrogated a royal title, and joined forces with Xiao Yan, who sent troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In eastern Jing Province the tribesman Fan An rallied men on Longshan, proclaimed himself king, and allied with Xiao Yan, who dispatched aid.

sentences.zh: 諸將擊討不利，乃以崇為使持節、散騎常侍、都督征蠻諸軍事，進號鎮南將軍，率步騎以討之。

translations.literal: When the generals' attacks fared poorly, Chong was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Commander of All Military Affairs for the Campaign Against the Barbarians, promoted to General Who Guards the South, and sent with infantry and cavalry to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: After other commanders failed, Chong was given the staff, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and commander of the barbarian campaign, promoted to General Who Guards the South, and sent with mixed forces against them.

sentences.zh: 崇分遣諸將，攻擊賊壘，連戰克捷，生擒樊安，進討西荊，諸蠻悉降。

translations.literal: Chong dispatched his generals to assault the rebel strongholds; victory followed victory; Fan An was captured alive; advancing west into Jing, all the tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent subordinates against the rebel camps, won battle after battle, took Fan An alive, and marched into western Jing until every tribe surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔以崇為使持節、兼侍中、東道大使，黜陟能否，著賞罰之稱。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chong Bearer of the Staff, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Grand Envoy of the Eastern Circuit to assess merit and demerit and establish reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was commissioned with the staff as concurrent palace attendant and eastern grand inspector to judge officials and fix standards of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 轉中護軍，出除散騎常侍、征南將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Defender of the Center, then appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Campaigns South, and Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He became Defender of the Center, then left office as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Campaigns South, and governor of Yang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「應敵制變，算非一途，救左擊右，疾雷均勢。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Meeting the enemy demands more than one method; saving the left by striking the right is like thunder equalizing force.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "To answer an enemy one path is not enough; relieving one flank by striking the other is like lightning that balances the field.

sentences.zh: 今朐山蟻寇，久結未殄，賊衍狡詐，或生詭劫，宜遣銳兵，備其不意。

translations.literal: Now the ant-like bandits at Qushan have long remained unextinguished; the brigand Yan is cunning and may launch sudden raids—sharp troops should be sent to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: The petty rebels at Qushan have lingered unconquered; Yan is deceitful and may strike by surprise—send elite troops to meet what he does not expect.

sentences.zh: 崇可都督淮南諸軍事，坐敦威重，遙運聲算。」

translations.literal: Chong shall command all military affairs in Huainan, seated in dignity and weight, directing strategy from afar."
translations.idiomatic: Let Chong command all Huainan forces, seated in authority and guiding operations from his post."

sentences.zh: 延昌初，加侍中、車騎將軍、都督江西諸軍事，刺史如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanchang era he was additionally made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of All Military Affairs west of the river; his governorship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanchang he was further made palace attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and commander of all forces west of the river, retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 先是，壽春縣人苟泰有子三歲，遇賊亡失，數年不知所在。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gou Tai of Shouchun County had a three-year-old son who was lost when bandits came; for years no one knew where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Gou Tai of Shouchun had lost his three-year-old son during a raid; for years the boy's whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 後見在同縣人趙奉伯家，泰以狀告。

translations.literal: Later the boy was seen in the home of Zhao Fengbo of the same county; Tai reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the child turned up in the household of a fellow townsman, Zhao Fengbo, and Tai filed a complaint.

sentences.zh: 各言己子，並有隣證，郡縣不能斷。

translations.literal: Each man claimed the boy as his son, and neighbors testified for both; the commandery and county could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Both men insisted the child was theirs, neighbors vouched for each side, and the local authorities could not settle the case.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「此易知耳。」

translations.literal: Chong said: "This is easy to know."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "That is simple to determine."

sentences.zh: 令二父與兒各在別處，禁經數旬，然後遣人告之曰：「君兒遇患，向已暴死，有教解禁，可出奔哀也。」

translations.literal: He had the two fathers and the child kept separately for several weeks, then sent someone to tell them: "Your son has fallen ill and has just died suddenly; there is an order lifting the restriction—you may go out to mourn."
translations.idiomatic: He separated the two men from the boy for weeks, then sent word: "Your son has taken ill and died suddenly; the restriction is lifted—come mourn him."

sentences.zh: 苟泰聞即號咷，悲不自勝；

translations.literal: Gou Tai at once wailed and could not contain his grief;
translations.idiomatic: Gou Tai burst into wailing and could not master his grief;

sentences.zh: 奉伯咨嗟而已，殊無痛意。

translations.literal: Fengbo sighed but showed no real pain.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo only sighed, with none of a father's anguish.

sentences.zh: 崇察知之，乃以兒還泰，詰奉伯詐狀。

translations.literal: Chong perceived the truth, returned the child to Tai, and interrogated Fengbo about his fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Chong saw through the ruse, gave the boy back to Tai, and pressed Fengbo until his deceit emerged.

sentences.zh: 奉伯乃款引云：「先亡一子，故妄認之。」

translations.literal: Fengbo then confessed: "I had lost a son earlier, so I falsely claimed this one."
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo admitted, "I had lost a child before, so I wrongly claimed this boy as mine."

sentences.zh: 又定州流人解慶賓兄弟，坐事俱徙揚州。

translations.literal: There were also the brothers Xie Qingbin of Dingzhou, exiled to Yangzhou for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: In another case the brothers Xie Qingbin of Dingzhou had been banished to Yangzhou for an offense.

sentences.zh: 弟思安背役亡歸，慶賓懼後役追責，規絕名貫，乃認城外死尸，詐稱其弟為人所殺，迎歸殯葬。

translations.literal: The younger brother Sian deserted his corvée and fled home; Qingbin feared later punishment for the labor draft, plotted to erase his registration, and identified a corpse outside the city, falsely claiming his brother had been murdered and bringing the body back for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Sian fled his labor duty; fearing pursuit, Qingbin schemed to strike his name from the rolls, claimed an unidentified corpse outside the walls as his brother murdered, and arranged a funeral.

sentences.zh: 頗類思安，見者莫辨。

translations.literal: It resembled Sian closely; none who saw it could tell the difference.
translations.idiomatic: The body closely resembled Sian, and witnesses could not distinguish them.

sentences.zh: 又有女巫陽氏自云見鬼，說思安被害之苦，飢渴之意。

translations.literal: A witch named Yang also claimed to see ghosts and described Sian's suffering when killed and his hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: A medium, Widow Yang, declared she saw spirits and told of Sian's torment in death, his hunger and thirst.

sentences.zh: 慶賓又誣疑同軍兵蘇顯甫、李蓋等所殺，經州訟之，二人不勝楚毒，各自款引。

translations.literal: Qingbin further accused fellow soldiers Su Xianfu and Li Gai of the murder; the case went to the prefecture, and the two, unable to endure torture, each confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin also accused comrades Su Xianfu and Li Gai; under torture at the prefecture both confessed.

sentences.zh: 獄將決竟，崇疑而停之。

translations.literal: As the case neared judgment Chong doubted and halted it.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of sentencing Chong harbored doubts and stayed the proceedings.

sentences.zh: 密遣二人非州內所識者，為從外來，詣慶賓告曰：「僕住在此州，去此三百。

translations.literal: Secretly he sent two men unknown in the prefecture, posing as travelers from outside, to tell Qingbin: "We lodge in this province, three hundred li from here.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly dispatched two strangers to Qingbin, saying, "We live in this region, three hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 比有一人見過寄宿，夜中共語，疑其有異，便即詰問，迹其由緒。

translations.literal: Recently a man stayed with us overnight; talking at night we found him suspicious and questioned him, tracing his story.
translations.idiomatic: A traveler lodged with us; talking late into the night we found him odd and pressed him for his history.

sentences.zh: 乃云是流兵背役逃走，姓解字思安。

translations.literal: He said he was a fugitive conscript surnamed Xie, styled Sian.
translations.idiomatic: He proved to be a deserter named Xie, courtesy name Sian.

sentences.zh: 時欲送官，苦見求及，稱有兄慶賓，今住揚州相國城內，嫂姓徐，君脫矜愍，為往報告，見申委曲，家兄聞此，必重相報，所有資財，當不愛惜。

translations.literal: We meant to hand him to the authorities, but he begged us hard, saying he had an elder brother Qingbin now living in the capital district of Yangzhou, his sister-in-law surnamed Xu; if you would pity him and report this, explaining everything, your brother will richly repay you and hold nothing back.
translations.idiomatic: We were about to turn him in, but he pleaded that his brother Qingbin lives in Yangzhou's capital district and his sister-in-law is surnamed Xu; show mercy, carry word to him, and he will reward you handsomely.

sentences.zh: 今但見質，若往不獲，送官何晚。

translations.literal: Keep him as pledge for now; if the errand fails, delivering him to officials will not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Hold him hostage meanwhile; if the message fails, there is still time to surrender him.

sentences.zh: 是故相造，指申此意。

translations.literal: That is why we have come to explain this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why we have sought you out.

sentences.zh: 君欲見雇幾何，當放賢弟。

translations.literal: Name your price and we will release your worthy brother.
translations.idiomatic: Name your fee and we will free your brother.

sentences.zh: 若其不信，可見隨看之。」

translations.literal: If you do not believe us, you may come and see for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt us, come see with your own eyes."

sentences.zh: 慶賓悵然失色，求其少停，當備財物。

translations.literal: Qingbin turned pale and asked them to wait while he gathered property.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin's face fell; he begged them to wait while he collected valuables.

sentences.zh: 此人具以報，崇攝慶賓問曰：「爾弟逃亡，何故妄認他尸？」

translations.literal: The men reported fully; Chong summoned Qingbin and asked: "Your brother fled—why did you falsely identify another corpse?"
translations.idiomatic: They reported back; Chong confronted Qingbin: "Your brother is alive—why claim a stranger's corpse?"

sentences.zh: 慶賓伏引。

translations.literal: Qingbin confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbin admitted everything.

sentences.zh: 更問蓋等，乃云自誣。

translations.literal: Questioned again, Gai and the others said they had falsely incriminated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Gai and the rest said under further questioning that they had lied.

sentences.zh: 數日之間，思安亦為人縛送。

translations.literal: Within days Sian was also bound and sent in.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Sian too was captured and delivered.

sentences.zh: 崇召女巫視之，鞭笞一百。

translations.literal: Chong summoned the witch for questioning and had her flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had the medium brought before him and ordered her beaten a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 崇斷獄精審，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Chong's judgments were all of this meticulous kind.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's courtroom discernment was invariably of this careful sort.

sentences.zh: 時有泉水湧於八公山頂；

translations.literal: At the time a spring gushed forth on the summit of Mount Bagong;
translations.idiomatic: About then a spring burst from the peak of Mount Bagong;

sentences.zh: 壽春城中有魚無數，從地湧出；

translations.literal: countless fish in Shouchun city surged up from the ground;
translations.idiomatic: innumerable fish welled up from the earth inside Shouchun;

sentences.zh: 野鴨羣飛入城，與鵲爭巢。

translations.literal: wild ducks flew into the city in flocks and fought magpies for nests.
translations.idiomatic: flocks of wild ducks entered the city and contested nests with magpies.

sentences.zh: 五月，大霖雨十有三日，大水入城，屋宇皆沒，崇與兵泊於城上。

translations.literal: In the fifth month great rains fell for thirteen days; floodwaters entered the city and every building was submerged; Chong and his soldiers moored on the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month torrential rain lasted thirteen days; the flood poured into the city until every house was underwater, and Chong and his troops clung to the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 水增未已，乃乘船附於女牆，城不沒者二板而已。

translations.literal: The water still rose; he then took to boats alongside the parapet, and only two courses of wall remained above the flood.
translations.idiomatic: As the waters kept rising he moored boats against the battlements; only two layers of wall still stood clear.

sentences.zh: 州府勸崇棄壽春，保北山。

translations.literal: The provincial and prefectural offices urged Chong to abandon Shouchun and hold the northern hills.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials pressed Chong to quit Shouchun and withdraw to the northern mountains.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「吾受國重恩，忝守藩岳，德薄招災，致此大水。

translations.literal: Chong said: "I have received the state's deep grace and am honored to guard this frontier command; my virtue is thin and has drawn this calamity, bringing on this great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "I owe the dynasty a profound debt and am entrusted with this border province; my failings have invited disaster and brought this flood upon us.

sentences.zh: 淮南萬里，繫于吾身。

translations.literal: Huainan stretches ten thousand li, and it hangs upon my person alone.
translations.idiomatic: All of Huainan hangs on me alone.

sentences.zh: 一旦動脚，百姓瓦解，揚州之地，恐非國物。

translations.literal: If I move my foot once, the people will collapse; the land of Yang Province may no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: One step from me and the people scatter—Yang Province may slip from the empire's grasp.

sentences.zh: 昔王尊慷慨，義感黃河，吾豈愛一軀，取愧千載。

translations.literal: In old times Wang Zun was resolute; his righteousness moved the Yellow River—how could I cherish one body and bring shame for a thousand years?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zun once steeled his heart and moved even the Yellow River; shall I cling to my own life and shame posterity?

sentences.zh: 但憐茲士庶，無辜同死，可桴筏隨高，人規自脫。

translations.literal: Yet I pity these officials and commoners, innocent yet doomed to die together; you may build rafts as the water rises and each devise his own escape.
translations.idiomatic: I pity these innocent people facing death with me—you may build rafts as the waters rise and save yourselves as you can.

sentences.zh: 吾必守死此城，幸諸君勿言。」

translations.literal: I shall die defending this city; I beg you all to say no more."
translations.idiomatic: I will hold this city unto death; please speak of it no further."

sentences.zh: 時州人裴絢等受蕭衍假豫州刺史，因乘大水，謀欲為亂，崇皆擊滅之。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Xuan and others of the province, invested by Xiao Yan as acting Governor of Yu, exploited the great flood to plot rebellion; Chong crushed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Pei Xuan and others, whom Xiao Yan had made acting governor of Yu, used the flood to plot revolt; Chong destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 崇以洪水為災，請罪解任。

translations.literal: Chong, holding the flood a calamity of his own making, requested punishment and resignation.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming himself for the flood, Chong asked to be punished and relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿居藩累年，威懷兼暢，資儲豐溢，足制勁寇。

translations.literal: The edict said: "You have governed your province for years; authority and kindness have both flourished, stores overflow, enough to master fierce enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "You have ruled your province for years with both awe and grace; your granaries are full and you can master strong foes.

sentences.zh: 然夏雨汎濫，斯非人力，何得以此辭解？

translations.literal: Yet the summer rains overflowed—this is not within human power; how can you resign on this account?
translations.idiomatic: But the summer rains were beyond human control—how can you resign for that?

sentences.zh: 今水涸路通，公私復業，便可繕甲積糧，修復城雉，勞恤士庶，務盡綏懷之略也。」

translations.literal: Now the waters have receded and roads are open; public and private life resume; repair armor, store grain, rebuild the walls, comfort officials and people, and carry out every policy of reassurance."
translations.idiomatic: The waters have fallen and roads are open again—repair arms and walls, store grain, comfort the people, and govern with every measure of reassurance."

sentences.zh: 崇又表請解州，詔報不聽。

translations.literal: Chong again memorialized to resign the governorship; the edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chong again asked to leave his post; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 是時非崇，則淮南不守矣。

translations.literal: At that time, without Chong, Huainan would not have been held.
translations.idiomatic: Without Chong, Huainan would have been lost.

sentences.zh: 崇沉深有將略，寬厚善御眾，在州凡經十年，常養壯士數千人，寇賊侵邊，所向摧破，號曰「臥虎」，賊甚憚之。

translations.literal: Chong was deep and possessed military strategy; generous and skilled at commanding men. In ten years as governor he always maintained several thousand stalwart warriors; when bandits raided the border he shattered all he met, and was called the "Crouching Tiger"—the enemy feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in counsel and skilled in war, generous with his men, Chong kept thousands of veterans ready through ten years as governor; raiders broke against him wherever he turned, earning the name "Crouching Tiger" and the enemy's dread.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍惡其久在淮南，屢設反間，無所不至，世宗雅相委重，衍無以措其姦謀。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan hated his long tenure in Huainan and repeatedly set intrigues, leaving no method untried; Emperor Shizong greatly trusted him, and Yan could not carry out his plots.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan resented Chong's long hold on Huainan and tried every intrigue, but Emperor Shizong's steadfast trust foiled him.

sentences.zh: 衍乃授崇車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、萬戶郡公，諸子皆為縣侯，欲以構崇。

translations.literal: Yan then invested Chong as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Same Honors as the Three Excellencies, and Duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery, making all his sons county marquises, intending to alienate Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then ennobled Chong with grand titles—General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, duke of a ten-thousand-household fief, and county marquisdoms for his sons—hoping to turn him traitor.

sentences.zh: 崇表言其狀，世宗屢賜璽書慰勉之。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized explaining the situation; Emperor Shizong repeatedly sent sealed letters to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong reported the matter; the emperor repeatedly wrote sealed letters of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 賞賜珍異，歲至五三，親待無與為比。

translations.literal: Gifts of rare treasures came five or six times a year; personal favor unmatched by any other.
translations.idiomatic: Rare gifts arrived five or six times a year; no one else enjoyed such personal favor.

sentences.zh: 衍每歎息，服世宗之能任崇也。

translations.literal: Yan sighed each time, admiring Shizong's ability to employ Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sighed each time, conceding Shizong's wisdom in trusting Chong.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐祚，褒賜衣馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, Chong was rewarded with robes and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Chong received robes and horses in reward.

sentences.zh: 及蕭衍遣其游擊將軍趙祖悅襲據西硤石，更築外城，逼徙緣淮之人於城內。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan sent his Mobile Commander Zhao Zuyue to seize and hold West Xiashi, rebuilding the outer wall and forcing people along the Huai to move inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent Mobile Commander Zhao Zuyue to seize West Xiashi, rebuild its outer wall, and drive Huai-dwellers into the city.

sentences.zh: 又遣二將昌義之、王神念率水軍泝淮而上，規取壽春。

translations.literal: He also sent two generals, Chang Yizhi and Wang Shennian, leading a navy up the Huai to plan the capture of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Two more generals, Chang Yizhi and Wang Shennian, sailed up the Huai to take Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 田道龍寇邊城，路長平寇五門，胡興茂寇開霍。

translations.literal: Tian Daolong raided the border fortresses; Lu Changping attacked Wumen; Hu Xingmao attacked Kaihuo.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Daolong struck border posts; Lu Changping hit Wumen; Hu Xingmao attacked Kaihuo.

sentences.zh: 揚州諸戍，皆被寇逼。

translations.literal: Every garrison in Yang Province was pressed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Every Yang garrison came under attack.

sentences.zh: 崇分遣諸將，與之相持。

translations.literal: Chong dispatched his generals to hold them in check.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent his commanders to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 密裝船艦二百餘艘，教之水戰，以待臺軍。

translations.literal: Secretly he fitted out more than two hundred warships and trained men in naval combat to await the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly fitted out over two hundred warships and drilled men for river fighting while awaiting imperial reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍霍州司馬田休等率眾寇建安，崇遣統軍李神擊走之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan's Huo Province aide Tian Xiu and others raided Jian'an, Chong sent Commander Li Shen to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Xiu of Huo Province raided Jian'an, Chong sent Li Shen to repulse him.

sentences.zh: 又命邊城戍主邵申賢要其走路，破之於濡水，俘斬三千餘人。

translations.literal: He also ordered the frontier commander Shao Shenxian to block their retreat and defeated them on the Ru River, capturing and killing more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commander Shao Shenxian ambushed their retreat at the Ru River, killing or capturing over three thousand.

sentences.zh: 靈太后璽書勞勉。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent a sealed letter of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent a sealed letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 許昌縣令兼紵麻戍主陳平玉南引衍軍，以戍歸之。

translations.literal: Chen Pingyu, magistrate of Xuchang and commander of the Zhuma garrison, led Yan's army south and surrendered the post.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchang magistrate Chen Pingyu, also commander of Zhuma garrison, defected to Yan and handed over his post.

sentences.zh: 崇自秋請援，表至十餘。

translations.literal: From autumn Chong pleaded for reinforcements; more than ten memorials arrived.
translations.idiomatic: From autumn onward Chong sent more than ten memorials begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 詔遣鎮南將軍崔亮救硤石，鎮東將軍蕭寶夤於衍堰上流決淮東注。

translations.literal: An edict sent General Who Guards the South Cui Liang to relieve Xiashi, and General Who Pacifies the East Xiao Baoyin to breach Yan's dam upstream and divert the Huai eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Cui Liang to relieve Xiashi and Xiao Baoyin to breach Yan's dam and divert the Huai eastward.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以諸將乖角，不相順赴，乃以尚書李平兼右僕射，持節節度之。

translations.literal: Because the generals worked at cross purposes and failed to coordinate, Minister Li Ping was made Concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat with staff authority to direct them.
translations.idiomatic: With commanders failing to coordinate, Li Ping was given staff authority to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 崇遣李神乘鬬艦百餘艘，沿淮與李平、崔亮合攻硤石。

translations.literal: Chong sent Li Shen with more than a hundred war junks down the Huai to join Li Ping and Cui Liang in assaulting Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent Li Shen with over a hundred war junks to join Li Ping and Cui Liang against Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 李神水軍克其東北外城，祖悅力屈乃降，語在平傳。

translations.literal: Li Shen's fleet took the northeastern outer wall; Zuyue, exhausted, surrendered—the account is in Li Ping's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen's fleet captured the northeastern outer wall; Zuyue surrendered—the full account is in Li Ping's biography.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，進號驃騎將軍、儀同三司，刺史、都督如故。

translations.literal: The court praised this and promoted Chong to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Same Honors as the Three Excellencies; his governorship and command were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted Chong to General of Agile Cavalry with the Same Honors as the Three Excellencies; his posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 衍淮堰未破，水勢日增。

translations.literal: Yan's Huai dam was not yet broken, and the water rose daily.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's dam still held and the waters rose daily.

sentences.zh: 崇乃於硤石戍間編舟為橋，北更立船樓十，各高三丈，十步置一籬，至兩岸，蕃板裝治，四箱解合，賊至舉用，不戰解下。

translations.literal: Chong then lashed boats into a bridge between the Xiashi garrisons; northward he erected ten ship-towers, each three zhang high, placing a palisade every ten paces to both banks, fitted with hinged boards in four sections that could be raised when enemies came and lowered without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chong lashed boats into a bridge between Xiashi garrisons and raised ten three-zhang ship-towers with palisades to both banks—hinged sections that could be raised against attack and lowered in peace.

sentences.zh: 又於樓船之北，連覆大船，東西竟水，防賊火栰。

translations.literal: North of the tower-ships he chained large vessels across the water east to west to block enemy fire-rafts.
translations.idiomatic: North of the towers he chained large ships across the river to block enemy fire-rafts.

sentences.zh: 又於八公山之東南，更起一城，以備大水，州人號曰魏昌城。

translations.literal: Southeast of Mount Bagong he built another city against the flood; the people called it Weichang City.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of Mount Bagong he built Weichang City against the flood.

sentences.zh: 崇累表解州，前後十餘上，肅宗乃以元志代之。

translations.literal: Chong repeatedly memorialized to resign the governorship, more than ten times in all; Suzong then replaced him with Yuan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten requests to resign, Suzong replaced Chong with Yuan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 尋除都督冀定瀛三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、冀州刺史，儀同如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commander of All Military Affairs in Ji, Ding, and Ying Provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Ji; his honors were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of Ji, Ding, and Ying, General of Agile Cavalry, and governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 不行。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He declined to go.

sentences.zh: 崇上表曰：

translations.literal: Chong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞世室明堂，顯於周夏；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Hall of the Epoch and the Bright Hall were displayed in Zhou and Xia;
translations.idiomatic: I have read that the Hall of the Epoch and Bright Hall shone in Zhou and Xia;

sentences.zh: 二黌兩學，盛自虞殷。

translations.literal: the two academies and paired schools flourished from Yu and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: the paired academies flourished under Yu and Yin.

sentences.zh: 所以宗配上帝，以著莫大之嚴；

translations.literal: By them the ancestral temple and Heaven were served, showing supreme solemnity;
translations.idiomatic: Through them the state worshipped Heaven and ancestors with supreme solemnity;

sentences.zh: 宣布下土，以彰則天之軌。

translations.literal: edicts were proclaimed to the realm, displaying the pattern of ruling as Heaven rules.
translations.idiomatic: edicts reached the realm, showing the pattern of ruling in Heaven's image.

sentences.zh: 養黃髮以詢格言，育青襟而敷典式，用能享國久長，風徽萬祀者也。

translations.literal: The white-haired were nourished to seek wise words; the green-collared were cultivated in classic models—thus states endured long and their fame lasted ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: The old were honored for wisdom, the young trained in classics—thus dynasties endured and their fame outlasted time.

sentences.zh: 故孔子稱巍巍乎其有成功，郁郁乎其有文章，此其盛矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said, "Lofty indeed was its accomplishment; rich indeed was its culture"—such was its greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Lofty its achievement, rich its culture"—such was that greatness.

sentences.zh: 爰暨亡秦，政失其道，坑儒滅學，以蔽黔首。

translations.literal: Down to the fallen Qin, government lost the Way; scholars were buried and learning extinguished to blind the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin fell, government lost the Way; scholars were buried and learning killed to blind the people.

sentences.zh: 國無黌序之風，野有非時之役，故九服分崩，祚終二世。

translations.literal: The state lacked academy wind; the countryside bore untimely corvée—thus the nine domains split and the throne ended in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Without academies in the capital and forced labor in the fields, the nine domains split and Qin died in two generations.

sentences.zh: 炎漢勃興，更修儒術，文景已降，禮樂復彰，化致昇平，治幾刑措。

translations.literal: The blazing Han rose, restored Confucian arts; from Emperors Wen and Jing onward ritual and music reappeared, transforming until ascendant peace, governing until punishments nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Han rose, restored learning; from Wen and Jing onward ritual and music returned until peace reigned and punishments nearly ceased.

sentences.zh: 故西京有六學之美，東都有三本之盛，莫不紛綸掩藹，響流無已。

translations.literal: Thus the Western Capital had the beauty of six academies; the Eastern Capital the splendor of three foundations—none failed to flourish abundantly, their renown flowing without end.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Capital boasted six academies; the Eastern three foundations—each age flourished and its fame never faded.

sentences.zh: 逮自魏晉，撥亂相因，[2]兵革之中，學校不絕，遺文燦然，方軌前代。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin, turmoil followed turmoil; [2] amid arms, schools never ceased; surviving texts blazed bright, matching former ages.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin through endless turmoil, [2] schools still survived amid war; texts endured, matching earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 仰惟高祖孝文皇帝稟聖自天，道鏡今古，徙馭嵩河，光宅函洛，模唐虞以革軌儀，規周漢以新品制，列教序於鄉黨，敦詩書於郡國。

translations.literal: Looking up to Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen, endowed with sagehood from Heaven, his Way mirroring past and present, moving the capital to the Song and Luo rivers, making his light dwell in Hangu and Luoyang, modeling Tang and Yu to reform rites, taking Zhou and Han to set new institutions, spreading education in villages, encouraging poetry and books in commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen, sage from Heaven, moved the capital to Luoyang, modeled Tang and Yu and Zhou and Han, spread education through villages and books through the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 使揖讓之禮，橫被於崎嶇；

translations.literal: Courtesy and yielding spread even over rugged lands;
translations.idiomatic: Rites of courtesy spread even to rugged lands;

sentences.zh: 歌詠之音，聲溢於仄陋。

translations.literal: songs and chants overflowed even humble lanes.
translations.idiomatic: songs overflowed even humble lanes.

sentences.zh: 但經始事殷，戎軒屢駕，未遑多就，弓劍弗追。

translations.literal: But founding tasks were urgent; the war-chariot often set out; there was no leisure to finish much; bow and sword could not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: But founding tasks pressed and campaigns interrupted—much remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 世宗統曆，聿遵先緒，永平之中，大興板築，續以水旱，戎馬生郊，雖逮為山，還停一簣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong inherited the precedent; in the Yongping era he greatly raised scaffolding; then flood and drought followed, war-horses in the suburbs—though a mountain was nearly built, one basket of earth still stopped short.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong followed his precedent; in Yongping he raised great works, but flood, drought, and war halted them one basket short of completion.

sentences.zh: 竊惟皇遷中縣，垂二十祀。

translations.literal: I reflect that since the imperial move to the central counties, nearly twenty years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly twenty years have passed since the move to the central plain.

sentences.zh: 而明堂禮樂之本，乃鬱荊棘之林；

translations.literal: Yet the root of Bright Hall ritual and music is choked with brambles;
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall, root of ritual and music, stands choked in brambles;

sentences.zh: 膠序德義之基，空盈牧竪之跡。

translations.literal: the foundation of the academy of virtue is empty save for shepherds' tracks.
translations.idiomatic: the academy foundation holds only shepherds' tracks.

sentences.zh: 城隍嚴固之重，闕塼石之工；

translations.literal: The weight of strong walls and moats lacks brick and stone work;
translations.idiomatic: Walls and moats lack proper brickwork;

sentences.zh: 墉堞顯望之要，少樓榭之飾。

translations.literal: the need for commanding towers and ramparts lacks pavilion ornament.
translations.idiomatic: towers and ramparts lack proper ornament.

sentences.zh: 加以風雨稍侵，漸致虧墜。

translations.literal: Added to this, wind and rain gradually encroach, and decay advances.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and rain have begun to erode what stands.

sentences.zh: 又府寺初營，頗亦壯美，然一造至今，更不修繕，廳宇凋朽，牆垣頹壞，皆非所謂追隆堂構，儀形萬國者也。

translations.literal: Also the initial government offices were quite magnificent, yet from one building to now they have never been repaired; halls decay, walls crumble—this is not what is called elevating the hall's structure and displaying form to ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: Government halls, once grand, have never been repaired; halls rot and walls fall—this is no image for the empire.

sentences.zh: 伏聞朝議，以高祖大造區夏，道侔姬文，擬祀明堂，式配上帝。

translations.literal: I have heard court discussion that because Gaozu greatly made the realm, his Way equal to King Wen, the Bright Hall is planned for worship and pairing with High God.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate holds that Gaozu, equal to King Wen, should be honored through Bright Hall worship paired with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今若基宇不修，仍同丘畎，即使高皇神享，闕於國陽，宗事之典，有聲無實。

translations.literal: If the foundations are not repaired and remain like field ditches, even if the high emperor's spirit is offered to, the national yang will lack it; the ancestral rite will have sound without substance.
translations.idiomatic: If foundations remain unrepaired like field ditches, ancestral rites will be sound without substance.

sentences.zh: 此臣子所以匪寧，億兆所以失望也。

translations.literal: This is why ministers and sons cannot rest easy and the hundred million are disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers cannot rest and the people are disappointed.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞官方授能，所以任事，事既任矣，酬之以祿。

translations.literal: I also hear that offices assign ability to assign tasks; once tasked, reward with salary.
translations.idiomatic: Offices assign ability to tasks and reward service with salary.

sentences.zh: 如此，上無曠官之譏，下絕尸素之謗。

translations.literal: Thus above there is no reproach for vacant posts; below no slander of idle stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Then none above reproaches empty posts nor below idle stipends.

sentences.zh: 今國子雖有學官之名，而無教授之實，何異兔絲燕麥，南箕北斗哉！

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Academy has the name of a teaching office but not the reality of instruction—how is it different from dodder on wheat, or the Southern Dipper and Northern Dipper?
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy has a name but no teaching—like dodder on wheat, or stars that measure nothing.

sentences.zh: 昔劉向有言：「王者宜興辟雍，陳禮樂，以風化天下。

translations.literal: Formerly Liu Xiang said: "A king should raise the Imperial Academy, display ritual and music, and transform the realm by custom.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "A king should raise the Imperial Academy, display ritual and music, and transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫禮樂所以養人，刑法所以殺人，而有司勤勤請定刑法，至於禮樂，則曰未敢，是則敢於殺人，不敢於養人也。」

translations.literal: Ritual and music nourish men; punishments kill men—yet officials diligently ask to fix punishments, while of ritual and music they say they dare not: thus they dare to kill but dare not nourish."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music nourish; punishments kill—yet officials rush to fix punishments while claiming ritual and music too bold: daring to kill but not to nourish."

sentences.zh: 臣以為當今四海清平，九服寧晏，經國要重，理應先營；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that today the four seas are clear, the nine domains tranquil; the weight of governing the state should be built first;
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is peaceful; statecraft should be built first;

sentences.zh: 脫復稽延，則劉向之言徵矣。

translations.literal: if delay continues, Liu Xiang's words will be verified.
translations.idiomatic: delay proves Liu Xiang right.

sentences.zh: 但事不兩興，須有進退。

translations.literal: But two great tasks cannot rise together; there must be advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Two great works cannot rise at once—choose advance or retreat.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚量，宜罷尚方雕靡之作，頗省永寧土木之功，并減瑤光材瓦之力，兼分石窟鐫琢之勞，及諸事役非急者，三時農隙，修此數條。

translations.literal: By my foolish measure, stop the lavish works of the Palace Ateliers, greatly reduce Yongning's earth-and-wood labor, also cut Yaoguang's timber and tile, share out the toil of grotto carving, and with all non-urgent labor, in the three seasons' farm gaps, repair these several items.
translations.idiomatic: Stop lavish palace crafts, cut Yongning construction, reduce Yaoguang timber, share grotto carving labor, and in farm seasons finish these tasks.

sentences.zh: 使辟雍之禮，蔚爾而復興；

translations.literal: Let Imperial Academy rites flourish and revive;
translations.idiomatic: Let academy rites flourish again;

sentences.zh: 諷誦之音，煥然而更作。

translations.literal: let chanting voices shine forth anew.
translations.idiomatic: let chanting voices rise anew.

sentences.zh: 美榭高墉，嚴壯於外；

translations.literal: Beautiful pavilions and high walls, stern without;
translations.idiomatic: Fair pavilions and high walls without;

sentences.zh: 槐宮棘宇，顯麗於中。

translations.literal: academy halls of pagoda-tree and thorn-wood, splendid within.
translations.idiomatic: academy halls, splendid within.

sentences.zh: 道發明令，[3]重遵鄉飲，敦進郡學，精課經業。

translations.literal: Issue bright edicts, [3] again honor village drinking, urge forward commandery schools, examine classic studies closely.
translations.idiomatic: Issue bright edicts, [3] restore village drinking rites, advance commandery schools, examine classics closely.

sentences.zh: 如此，則元、凱可得之於上序，游夏可致之於下國，豈不休歟！

translations.literal: Thus Yuan and Kai could be obtained in the upper academies, and You and Xia brought to lesser states—would this not be glorious!
translations.idiomatic: Then great scholars would fill upper academies and teachers lesser states—would it not be glorious!

sentences.zh: 誠知佛理淵妙，含識所宗，然比之治要，容可小緩。

translations.literal: I truly know Buddhist doctrine is profound and all conscious beings revere it; yet compared with governing essentials it may be slightly deferred.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist doctrine is profound and revered; yet beside governing essentials it may wait.

sentences.zh: 苟使魏道熙緝，元首唯康，爾乃經營，未為晚也。

translations.literal: If Wei's Way is bright and the sovereign alone is well, then building afterward is not late.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei's Way shines and the ruler is secure, building later is not too late.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「省表，具悉體國之誠。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Having read the memorial, I fully understand your loyalty to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Your memorial shows true loyalty to the state.

sentences.zh: 配饗大禮，為國之本，比以戎馬在郊，未遑修繕。

translations.literal: The great rite of paired offering is the root of the state; lately war-horses were in the suburbs and repair could not be hurried.
translations.idiomatic: The great offering rite is the state's root; war lately prevented repair.

sentences.zh: 今四表晏寧，年和歲稔，當敕有司別議經始。」

translations.literal: Now the four borders are calm, years and harvests are rich; the relevant offices should separately discuss founding."
translations.idiomatic: Now borders are calm and harvests rich; offices shall plan the work."

sentences.zh: 除中書監、驃騎大將軍，儀同如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and General of Agile Cavalry; his honors were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Secretariat and General of Agile Cavalry with honors unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又授右光祿大夫，出為使持節、侍中、都督定幽燕瀛四州諸軍事、本將軍、定州刺史，儀同如故。

translations.literal: He was also given Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander of All Military Affairs in Ding, You, Yan, and Ying Provinces, retaining his general's rank as Governor of Ding; honors unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and sent to command Ding, You, Yan, and Ying as governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 徵拜尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍，驃騎、儀同如故。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; General of Agile Cavalry and honors unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Left Vice Director with Regular Attendant rank; honors unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, additionally Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 崇在官和厚，明於決斷，受納辭訟，必理在可推，始為下筆，不徒爾收領也。

translations.literal: In office Chong was harmonious and generous, clear in judgment; in receiving lawsuits he wrote only when reason could be weighed—never merely collecting papers.
translations.idiomatic: In office Chong was fair and decisive; he ruled on lawsuits only when reason was clear, never merely shuffling papers.

sentences.zh: 然性好財貨，販肆聚斂，家資巨萬，營求不息。

translations.literal: Yet he loved wealth, traded and hoarded; family assets reached tens of thousands, and he pursued gain without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved wealth, traded and hoarded without cease until his estate reached vast sums.

sentences.zh: 子世哲為相州刺史，亦無清白狀。

translations.literal: His son Shizhe as Governor of Xiang Province likewise had no record of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhe as Xiang governor likewise lacked integrity.

sentences.zh: 鄴洛市鄽，收擅其利，為時論所鄙。

translations.literal: In the markets of Ye and Luoyang he monopolized profit and was despised by public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He monopolized Ye and Luoyang markets and was scorned for it.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瓌率眾犯塞，詔崇以本官都督北討諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: When the Rouran ruler Anagui led masses to raid the frontier, an edict made Chong, in his existing office, Commander of All Northern Campaign Military Affairs to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Rouran ruler Anagui raided the frontier, Chong was ordered to command the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 崇辭於顯陽殿，戎服武飾，志氣奮揚，時年六十九，幹力如少。

translations.literal: Chong took leave at Xianyang Hall in martial dress and arms, spirit soaring; he was sixty-nine, yet vigor like youth.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave at Xianyang Hall in full armor at sixty-nine, his spirit burned like a young man's.

sentences.zh: 肅宗目而壯之，朝廷莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Suzong looked and found him imposing; the court all praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong looked on approvingly; the whole court praised him.

sentences.zh: 崇遂出塞三千餘里，不及賊而還。

translations.literal: Chong then went beyond the frontier more than three thousand li, failed to catch the enemy, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chong marched over three thousand li beyond the frontier, failed to overtake the enemy, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 後北鎮破落汗拔陵反叛，所在響應。

translations.literal: Later Poluohan Baling of the Northern Garrison rebelled, and responses rose everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Later Baling of Broken Locust Han rebelled at the Northern Garrison, and uprisings spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍、臨淮王彧大敗於五原，安北將軍李叔仁尋敗於白道，賊眾日甚。

translations.literal: General Who Campaigns North and Prince of Linhuai, Yu, was greatly defeated at Wuyuan; General Who Pacifies the North Li Shuren was soon defeated at Baidao—the rebel host grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Linhuai, General Who Campaigns North, was routed at Wuyuan; Li Shuren was beaten at Baidao—and the rebels swelled daily.

sentences.zh: 詔引丞相、令、僕、尚書、侍中、黃門於顯陽殿，詔曰：「朕比以鎮人搆逆，登遣都督臨淮王克時除翦。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the Chancellor, Director, Vice Directors, Ministers, Attendants, and Yellow Gate officials to Xianyang Hall and said: "We lately because garrison men plotted rebellion dispatched Commander Prince of Linhuai to destroy them in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the high ministers to Xianyang Hall and said, "When garrison troops rebelled We sent Prince Yu of Linhuai to crush them promptly.

sentences.zh: 軍屆五原，前鋒失利，二將殞命，兵士挫衂。

translations.literal: The army reached Wuyuan; the vanguard failed; two generals lost their lives; soldiers were broken.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyuan the vanguard failed, two generals died, and the army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 又武川乖防，復陷凶手。

translations.literal: Also Wuchuan's defenses failed, and the murderers seized it again.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchuan's defenses collapsed and the killers took it again.

sentences.zh: 恐賊勢侵淫，寇連恒朔。

translations.literal: We fear the rebel momentum will spread and raids will link Heng and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: We fear the rebellion will spread and raids will sweep Heng and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 金陵在彼，夙夜憂惶。

translations.literal: Jinling lies yonder; day and night We are anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling lies ahead; We worry day and night.

sentences.zh: 諸人宜陳良策，以副朕懷。」

translations.literal: You all should offer good plans to fulfill Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Propose good strategies to meet Our need."

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書元脩義曰：「強寇充斥，事須得討。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Xiuyi said: "Strong bandits fill the land; the matter must be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yuan Xiuyi said, "Bandits fill the land; they must be crushed.

sentences.zh: 臣謂須得重貴，鎮壓恒朔，總彼師旅，備衞金陵。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that a man of heavy rank is needed to hold down Heng and Shuo, command those armies, and guard Jinling."
translations.idiomatic: We need a man of high rank to hold Heng and Shuo, command the armies, and guard Jinling."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「去歲阿那瓌叛逆，遣李崇令北征，崇遂長驅塞北，返旆榆關，此亦一時之盛。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Last year Anagui rebelled; We sent Li Chong on a northern campaign; Chong then drove deep into the northern frontier and returned his banners at Yugu Pass—this too was a moment of glory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Last year We sent Li Chong north; he drove deep into the frontier and returned via Yugu—a moment of glory.

sentences.zh: 崇乃上表求改鎮為州，罷削舊貫。

translations.literal: Chong then memorialized asking to change garrisons into provinces and abolish old registers.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had memorialized to turn garrisons into provinces and erase old registers.

sentences.zh: 朕于時以舊典難革，不許其請。

translations.literal: We at the time, because old statutes were hard to change, did not grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: We refused because old statutes were hard to change.

sentences.zh: 尋李崇此表，開諸鎮非異之心，致有今日之事。

translations.literal: Soon Li Chong's memorial opened the garrisons' hearts of alienation and brought today's affair.
translations.idiomatic: That memorial planted alienation in the garrisons and led to today's disaster.

sentences.zh: 但既往難追，為復略論此耳。

translations.literal: But the past cannot be pursued; We merely discuss this in brief.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be undone; We mention it only in passing.

sentences.zh: 朕以李崇國戚望重，器識英斷，意欲還遣崇行，總督三軍，揚旌恒朔，除彼羣盜。

translations.literal: We, because Li Chong is a royal in-law of heavy repute, talent and judgment bright and decisive, intend to send Chong again, commanding all three armies, raising banners in Heng and Shuo, and removing those bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong is a royal in-law of weight and talent; We intend to send him again to command three armies in Heng and Shuo and destroy the bandits.

sentences.zh: 諸人謂可爾以不？」

translations.literal: Do you all think this can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you approve?"

sentences.zh: 僕射蕭寶夤等曰：「陛下以舊都在北，憂慮金陵，臣等實懷悚息。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xiao Baoyin and others said: "Your Majesty, because the old capital is in the north, worries for Jinling; we are truly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin said, "Your Majesty rightly fears for Jinling with the old capital in the north.

sentences.zh: 李崇德位隆重，社稷之臣，陛下此遣，實合羣望。」

translations.literal: Li Chong's virtue and rank are solemn; he is a pillar of the state; this dispatch truly fits the multitude's hope."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong is a pillar of the state; this appointment fits everyone's hope."

sentences.zh: 崇啟曰：「臣實無用，猥蒙殊寵，位妨賢路，遂充北伐。

translations.literal: Chong submitted: "Your servant is truly useless, yet undeservedly received special favor; my rank blocks the path of the worthy, and thus I filled the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "I am unworthy yet overfavored; I blocked worthies and failed the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 徒勞將士，無勳而還，慚負聖朝，於今莫已。

translations.literal: I exhausted officers and soldiers, returned without merit, and shamed the holy court—shame to this day without end.
translations.idiomatic: I wasted soldiers and returned without merit, shaming the court without end.

sentences.zh: 臣以六鎮幽垂，與賊接對，鳴柝聲弦，弗離旬朔。

translations.literal: Your servant, because the six garrisons lie in remote shadow, face the enemy, and alarm drums and bowstrings never leave a ten-day month.
translations.idiomatic: The six garrisons face the enemy constantly; alarms never cease.

sentences.zh: 州名差重於鎮，謂實可悅彼心，使聲教日揚，微塵去塞。

translations.literal: A province name is somewhat heavier than a garrison; I held it would truly please their hearts, make Our teaching daily spread, and dust depart the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I thought renaming garrisons as provinces would win hearts and spread civilization to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 豈敢導此凶源，開生賊意。

translations.literal: How dare I guide this source of disaster and open living bandit intent?
translations.idiomatic: I never meant to sow rebellion.

sentences.zh: 臣之愆負，死有餘責。

translations.literal: Your servant's fault and burden—death would still leave guilt.
translations.idiomatic: My guilt deserves death.

sentences.zh: 屬陛下慈寬，賜全腰領。

translations.literal: Thanks to Your Majesty's kindness and breadth, I was granted my waist and neck whole.
translations.idiomatic: Your mercy spared my life.

sentences.zh: 今更遣臣北行，正是報恩改過，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Now to send your servant north again is exactly repaying grace and correcting fault; I dare not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: To march north again is my chance to repay grace and amend fault; I dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 但臣年七十，自惟老疾，不堪敵場，更願英賢，收功盛日。」

translations.literal: But your servant is seventy; I reflect on old age and illness, unfit for the battlefield; I would rather an able man gather merit in a flourishing day."
translations.idiomatic: But I am seventy, ill and unfit for battle; let an able man win glory instead."

sentences.zh: 於是詔崇以本官加使持節、開府、北討大都督，撫軍將軍崔暹，鎮軍將軍、廣陵王淵皆受崇節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict made Chong, in his existing office, additionally Bearer of the Staff, Opener of the Office, and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign; General Who Pacifies the Army Cui Xuan and General Who Guards the Army Prince of Guangling, Yuan, all received Chong's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was made Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign with staff authority; Cui Xuan and Prince Yuan of Guangling served under him.

sentences.zh: 又詔崇子光祿大夫神軌，假平北將軍，隨崇北討。

translations.literal: An edict also made Chong's son Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Shengui acting General Who Pacifies the North to follow Chong north.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shengui was made acting General Who Pacifies the North and accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 崇至五原，崔暹大敗于白道之北，賊遂并力攻崇。

translations.literal: Chong reached Wuyuan; Cui Xuan was greatly defeated north of Baidao; the bandits then combined strength to attack Chong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyuan Cui Xuan was routed north of Baidao; the rebels then massed against Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇與廣陵王淵力戰，累破賊眾，相持至冬，乃引還平城。

translations.literal: Chong and Prince of Guangling Yuan fought hard, repeatedly breaking the rebel host; they held each other until winter, then withdrew to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Prince Yuan fought through winter, repeatedly defeating rebels, then withdrew to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 淵表崇長史祖瑩詐增功級，盜沒軍資。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized that Chong's chief clerk Zu Ying falsely inflated merit grades and embezzled army supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan accused Chong's chief clerk Zu Ying of inflating merit rolls and embezzling supplies.

sentences.zh: 崇坐免官爵，徵還，以後事付淵。

translations.literal: Chong was punished by removal of office and rank, summoned back; later affairs were entrusted to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was stripped of rank and recalled; Yuan took over.

sentences.zh: 後徐州刺史元法僧以彭城南叛，時除安樂王鑒為徐州刺史以討法僧，為法僧所敗，單馬奔歸。

translations.literal: Later Xu Governor Yuan Faseng rebelled with Pengcheng to the south; at the time Prince of Anle Jian was appointed Xu Governor to suppress Faseng and was defeated by Faseng, fleeing back alone on one horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng, Prince Jian of Anle was sent against him, defeated, and fled alone.

sentences.zh: 乃詔復崇官爵，為徐州大都督，節度諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict then restored Chong's office and rank and made him Grand Commander of Xuzhou, directing all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's rank was restored and he was made grand commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會崇疾篤，乃以衞將軍、安豐王延明代之。

translations.literal: When Chong's illness grew grave, General of the Guard Prince of Anfeng Yan was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: As Chong fell gravely ill, Prince Yan of Anfeng replaced him.

sentences.zh: 改除開府、相州刺史，侍中、將軍、儀同並如故。

translations.literal: He was reassigned Opener of the Office and Governor of Xiang; Palace Attendant, general, and honors were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to open an office and govern Xiang, retaining his honors.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年薨於位，時年七十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang he died in office at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Xiaochang 1 at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、雍州刺史，諡曰武康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Yong; posthumous name Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Education, and Yong governor, titled Wukang.

sentences.zh: 後重贈太尉公，增邑一千戶，餘如故。

translations.literal: Later he was again posthumously given Grand Duke of the Ministry of War with fief increased by one thousand households; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously made Grand Minister of War with a thousand added households.

sentences.zh: 長子世哲，性輕率，供奉豪侈。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shizhe was by nature rash, extravagant in provision and luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Shizhe was rash and lived in luxury.

sentences.zh: 少經征役，頗有將用。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through campaigns and had considerable military usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: He saw campaigns in youth and proved useful in war.

sentences.zh: 自司徒中兵參軍，超為征虜將軍、驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: From Army Controller of the Ministry of Education he was abruptly made General Who Captures the Enemy and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: From a staff post he leapt to General Who Captures the Enemy and General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋遷後將軍，為三關別將，討羣蠻，大破之，斬蕭衍龍驤將軍文思之等。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Rear General, made Separate Commander of the Three Passes, suppressed tribal barbarians, greatly defeated them, and beheaded Xiao Yan's General of Dragon Cavalry Wensizhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Made Separate Commander of the Three Passes, he crushed barbarians and killed Xiao Yan's General Wensizhi.

sentences.zh: 還拜鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he became Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations.

sentences.zh: 性傾巧，善事人，亦以貨賂自達。

translations.literal: By nature he was crafty at inclining and good at pleasing men; he also advanced through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty and skilled at pleasing men, he also bought advancement.

sentences.zh: 高肇、劉騰之處勢也，皆與親善，故世號為「李錐」。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao and Liu Teng held power he was close to both, so the age called him "Li Awl."
translations.idiomatic: Close to Gao Zhao and Liu Teng in power, he was nicknamed "Li Awl."

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，遷宗正卿，加平南將軍，轉大司農卿，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Suzong's reign he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Clan, additionally General Who Pacifies the South, then Grand Minister of Agriculture, retaining his general's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Suzong's reign he became Director of the Imperial Clan, then Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 又改授太僕卿，加鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: He was again reassigned Grand Master of the Stud, additionally General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of the Stud and General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 尋出為相州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Xiang; his general's rank was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Xiang as before.

sentences.zh: 世哲至州，斥逐細人，遷徙佛寺，逼買其地，廣興第宅，百姓患之。

translations.literal: When Shizhe reached the province he drove out common people, moved Buddhist temples, forced purchase of their land, and widely raised mansions—the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiang governor he expelled commoners, seized temple lands, and built mansions—the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 崇北征之後，徵兼太常卿。

translations.literal: After Chong's northern campaign he was summoned as Concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong's northern campaign he was recalled as Concurrent Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 御史高道穆毀發其宅，表其罪過。

translations.literal: Censor Gao Daomu demolished his mansion and memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Daomu tore down his mansion and reported his crimes.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮西將軍、涇州刺史，賜爵衞國子。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the West and Governor of Jing; he was given the noble rank Marquis of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became General Who Guards the West and Jing governor, ennobled as Marquis of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 正光五年七月卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Zhengguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Zhengguang 5.

sentences.zh: 賻帛五百匹、朝服一襲，贈散騎常侍、衞將軍、吏部尚書、冀州刺史，子如故。

translations.literal: Five hundred bolts of silk and one set of court robes were sent as funeral gifts; posthumously he was given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of the Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Ji; his son's rank was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts of five hundred bolts of silk were sent; posthumously he was made Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Ji governor.

sentences.zh: 世哲弟神軌，受父爵陳留侯。

translations.literal: Shizhe's younger brother Shengui inherited his father's rank as Marquis of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Shengui inherited the Chenliu marquisate.

sentences.zh: 自給事中，稍遷員外常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: From Attendant Within he was gradually promoted to Outside Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: From Attendant Within he rose to Outside Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 累出征討，頗有將領之氣。

translations.literal: Repeatedly on campaign he had considerable commander's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated campaigns gave him a commander's bearing.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，為靈太后寵遇，勢傾朝野，時云見幸帷幄，與鄭儼為雙，時人莫能明也。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang he was favored by Empress Dowager Ling; his power tilted court and countryside; the age said he was intimate within the curtained bedchamber, paired with Zheng Yan—no one could clarify it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang Empress Dowager Ling favored him; rumor paired him with Zheng Yan in imperial intimacy.

sentences.zh: 頻遷征東將軍、武衞將軍、給事黃門侍郎，常領中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to General Who Campaigns East, General of Martial Guard, and Attendant of the Yellow Gate Within the Service; he often held Chief Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through eastern campaign commands to Yellow Gate Attendant and often held Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史、安樂王鑒據州反，詔神軌與都督源子邕等討平之。

translations.literal: When Xiang Governor Prince of Anle Jian held the province in rebellion, an edict sent Shengui with Commander Yuan Ziyong and others to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jian of Anle rebelled in Xiang, Shengui and Yuan Ziyong suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，蠻帥李洪扇動諸落，伊闕已東，至於鞏縣，多被燒劫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai the barbarian chief Li Hong stirred the tribes; east of Yique to Gong County many were burned and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wutai barbarian chief Li Hong ravaged from Yique east to Gong County.

sentences.zh: 詔神軌為都督，破平之。

translations.literal: An edict made Shengui Commander; he broke and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Made commander, he crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之向洛也，復為大都督，率眾禦之。
