translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang he was again made Grand Commander, leading masses to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang he was again made Grand Commander to resist.

sentences.zh: 出至河橋，值北中不守，遂便退還。

translations.literal: He went out to Heqiao; when the northern center was not held he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao, finding the northern center lost, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋與百官候駕於河陰，仍遇害焉。

translations.literal: Soon with the hundred officials he awaited the imperial carriage at Heyin and there met his death.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting for the emperor at Heyin with the court, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 建義初，贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、司空公、相州刺史，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was posthumously given Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Xiang; posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Xiang governor, titled Lie.

sentences.zh: 崔亮，字敬儒，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Liang, courtesy name Jingru, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang, styled Jingru, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父元孫，劉駿尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Yuansun was a Secretariat Gentleman under Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuansun served Liu Jun as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 劉彧之僭立也，彧青州刺史沈文秀阻兵叛之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu usurped the throne, Yu's Qing Governor Shen Wenxiu raised troops and rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu usurped the throne, Shen Wenxiu of Qing Province rebelled.

sentences.zh: 彧使元孫討文秀，為文秀所害。

translations.literal: Yu sent Yuansun to suppress Wenxiu; Yuansun was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Yuansun against Wenxiu; Wenxiu killed him.

sentences.zh: 亮母房氏，攜亮依冀州刺史崔道固於歷城，道固即亮之叔祖也。

translations.literal: Liang's mother Lady Fang carried Liang to rely on Ji Governor Cui Daogu at Licheng; Daogu was Liang's granduncle.
translations.idiomatic: Mother Lady Fang brought Liang to granduncle Cui Daogu, Ji governor at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 及慕容白曜之平三齊，內徙桑乾，為平齊民。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao pacified the Three Qi, they were moved inward to Sanggan as Pacified-Qi commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao pacified the Three Qi they were resettled at Sanggan as Pacified-Qi people.

sentences.zh: 時年十歲，常依季父幼孫，居家貧，傭書自業。

translations.literal: At the time he was ten years old, always relying on his father's younger brother Yousun; the household was poor and he copied books for a living.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he lived with uncle Yousun in poverty, copying books for a living.

sentences.zh: 時隴西李沖當朝任事，亮從兄光往依之，謂亮曰：「安能久事筆硯，而不往託李氏也？

translations.literal: At the time Li Chong of Longxi held court office; Liang's older cousin Guang went to rely on him and said to Liang: "How can you long serve brush and inkstone and not go entrust yourself to the Li family?
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Guang, serving Li Chong of Longxi, urged Liang: "Why copy books forever instead of joining the Lis?

sentences.zh: 彼家饒書，因可得學。」

translations.literal: That house is rich in books; thereby you can study."
translations.idiomatic: Their house is full of books—you could learn there."

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「弟妹飢寒，豈可獨飽？

translations.literal: Liang said: "Younger siblings are hungry and cold—how can I alone be full?
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "My siblings are hungry—how can I eat alone?

sentences.zh: 自可觀書於市，安能看人眉睫乎！」

translations.literal: One can view books in the market; how can I watch other people's eyelashes!"
translations.idiomatic: I can read in the market; I won't live at others' whim!"

sentences.zh: 光言之於沖，沖召亮與語，因謂亮曰：「比見卿先人相命論，使人胸中無復怵迫之念。

translations.literal: Guang spoke of this to Chong; Chong summoned Liang to converse and therefore said to Liang: "Lately seeing your forefather's physiognomy treatise, it made one's breast free of pressing anxiety again.
translations.idiomatic: Guang told Li Chong, who summoned Liang and said, "Your forefather's physiognomy text once eased my mind.

sentences.zh: 今遂亡本，卿能記之不？」

translations.literal: Now the original is lost; can you remember it?"
translations.idiomatic: The book is lost—can you recite it?"

sentences.zh: 亮即為誦之，涕淚交零，聲韻不異。

translations.literal: Liang at once recited it; tears crossed and fell; tone and rhythm were not different.
translations.idiomatic: Liang recited it through tears with perfect tone and rhythm.

sentences.zh: 沖甚奇之，迎為館客。

translations.literal: Chong greatly marveled and welcomed him as a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong marveled and took him as house guest.

sentences.zh: 沖謂其兄子彥曰：「大崔生寬和篤雅，汝宜友之；

translations.literal: Chong told his brother's son Yan: "Elder Cui is generous, steady, and elegant—you should befriend him;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong told his nephew Yan, "Elder Cui is generous and steady—befriend him;

sentences.zh: 小崔生峭整清徹，汝宜敬之。

translations.literal: Younger Cui is sharp, orderly, clear, and penetrating—you should respect him.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Cui is sharp and clear—respect him.

sentences.zh: 二人終將大至。」

translations.literal: Both men will ultimately reach great heights."
translations.idiomatic: Both will rise far."

sentences.zh: 沖薦之為中書博士。

translations.literal: Chong recommended him as Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong recommended him as Secretariat Erudite.

sentences.zh: 轉議郎，尋遷尚書二千石郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reviewer; soon he was promoted to Gentleman of the Two Thousand-Dan Bureau of the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: He became Reviewer, then Gentleman of the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 高祖在洛，欲創革舊制，選置百官，謂羣臣曰：「與朕舉一吏部郎，必使才望兼允者，給卿三日假。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu at Luoyang wished to create and reform old institutions and select and place the hundred offices; he told the ministers: "Recommend one Director of Personnel for Us who must make talent and repute both fulfilled; We give you three days' leave."
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Gaozu told ministers, "Find a Director of Personnel combining talent and reputation—you have three days."

sentences.zh: 又一日，高祖曰：「朕已得之，不煩卿輩也。」

translations.literal: Another day Gaozu said: "We have already obtained him; no need to trouble you all."
translations.idiomatic: Next day he said, "I have him; trouble yourselves no more."

sentences.zh: 馳驛徵亮兼吏部郎。

translations.literal: By post relay he summoned Liang as Concurrent Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was summoned by post as Concurrent Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 俄為太子中舍人，遷中書侍郎，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was Crown Prince Household Attendant, transferred to Secretariat Vice Director, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Crown Prince Attendant, then Secretariat Vice Director and Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 亮雖歷顯任，其妻不免親事舂簸。

translations.literal: Though Liang passed through prominent posts, his wife did not escape personally handling pounding and winnowing.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held high office, his wife still pounded grain herself.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，嘉其清貧，詔帶野王令。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard this, praised his clean poverty, and ordered him to hold concurrently the magistracy of Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised his poverty and made him concurrent magistrate of Yewang.

sentences.zh: 世宗親政，遷給事黃門侍郎，仍兼吏部郎，領青州大中正。

translations.literal: When Shizong personally governed he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate Within the Service, still concurrently Director of Personnel, and held Grand Assessor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took power he became Yellow Gate Attendant, still directing Personnel and assessing Qing.

sentences.zh: 亮自參選事，垂將十年，廉慎明決，為尚書郭祚所委，[4]每云：「非崔郎中，選事不辦。」

translations.literal: From the time Liang participated in selection affairs, nearly ten years passed; he was incorrupt, cautious, clear, and decisive; he was entrusted by Minister Guo Zuo, [4] who always said: "Without Vice Director Cui, selection affairs cannot be handled."
translations.idiomatic: For nearly ten years in Personnel he was incorrupt and decisive; Minister Guo Zuo [4] said, "Without Cui, Personnel cannot function."

sentences.zh: 尋除散騎常侍，仍為黃門。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and still held the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry while keeping the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 遷度支尚書，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue and held concurrently Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Revenue and concurrent Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 自遷都之後，經略四方，又營洛邑，費用甚廣。

translations.literal: After the move of the capital, governing the four directions and building Luoyang cost greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved, campaigns and building Luoyang cost enormously.

sentences.zh: 亮在度支，別立條格，歲省億計。

translations.literal: Liang at Revenue established separate regulations, saving hundreds of millions yearly.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of Revenue Liang set new rules saving hundreds of millions each year.

sentences.zh: 又議修汴蔡二渠，以通邊運，公私賴焉。

translations.literal: He also proposed repairing the Bian and Cai canals to open frontier transport; public and private both relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed repairing the Bian and Cai canals for frontier transport, to public and private benefit.

sentences.zh: 侍中、廣平王懷以母弟之親，左右不遵憲法，敕亮推治。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Prince of Guangping Huai, by maternal-brother kinship, had attendants who did not obey law; an order directed Liang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Guangping's attendants broke the law; Liang was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 世宗禁懷不通賓客者久之。

translations.literal: Shizong forbade Huai to receive guests for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong barred Huai from receiving guests for a long while.

sentences.zh: 後因宴集，懷恃親使忿，欲陵突亮。

translations.literal: Later at a banquet Huai, relying on kinship, grew angry and wished to overwhelm Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At a later banquet Huai, relying on kinship, tried to browbeat Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮乃正色責之，即起於世宗前，脫冠請罪，遂拜辭欲出。

translations.literal: Liang sternly rebuked him, then rose before Shizong, removed his cap to ask punishment, bowed farewell and wished to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Liang rebuked him, then before Shizong removed his cap to accept punishment and started to leave.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「廣平粗疏，向來又醉，卿之所悉，何乃如此也？」

translations.literal: Shizong said: "Guangping is coarse and lately was drunk too; you know this—why act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "Guangping is rough and was drunk—you know this; why take it so hard?"

sentences.zh: 遂詔亮復坐，令懷謝焉。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Liang to sit again and made Huai apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was told to sit again and Huai was made to apologize.

sentences.zh: 亮外雖方正，內亦承候時情，宣傳左右郭神安頗被世宗識遇，以弟託亮，亮引為御史，及神安敗後，因集禁中，世宗令兼侍中盧昶宣旨責亮曰：「在法官何故受左右囑請？」

translations.literal: Outwardly Liang was upright, inwardly he also accommodated the times; attendant Guo Shen'an was much favored by Shizong and entrusted his younger brother to Liang; Liang brought him in as censor; after Shen'an's fall, at an assembly in the palace Shizong had Concurrent Attendant Lu Chang proclaim and rebuke Liang: "As a law officer why accept requests from attendants?"
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly upright, Liang also accommodated the times; he made Guo Shen'an's brother a censor, and after Shen'an fell Shizong had Lu Chang rebuke him for taking attendants' favors."

sentences.zh: 亮拜謝而已，無以上對。

translations.literal: Liang bowed in apology only, with nothing to answer above.
translations.idiomatic: Liang could only bow and had no reply.

sentences.zh: 轉都官尚書，又轉七兵，領廷尉卿，加散騎常侍，中正如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, then to the Seventh Bureau, holding concurrently Director of the Court of Justice, additionally Regular Attendant; Grand Assessor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Punishments, then Seventh Bureau minister, concurrent Court of Justice director and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史元昞撫御失和，詔亮馳驛安撫。

translations.literal: Xu Governor Yuan Bing's governance failed in harmony; an edict sent Liang by post relay to soothe.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu governor Yuan Bing lost control, Liang was sent by post to soothe the province.

sentences.zh: 亮至，劾昞，處以大辟，勞賚綏慰，百姓帖然。

translations.literal: Liang arrived, impeached Bing, punished with great execution, rewarded and comforted with labor gifts—the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Liang impeached Bing, sentenced him to death, rewarded the people, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 除安西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Yong governor.

sentences.zh: 城北渭水淺不通船，行人艱阻。

translations.literal: North of the city the Wei River was shallow and boats could not pass; travelers found it hard.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city the Wei was too shallow for boats and travel was hard.

sentences.zh: 亮謂僚佐曰：「昔杜預乃造河梁，況此有異長河，且魏晉之日亦自有橋，吾今決欲營之。」

translations.literal: Liang told his staff: "Formerly Du Yu made a river bridge; how much more this differs from the long river—and Wei and Jin days also had their bridge; I now resolve to build it."
translations.idiomatic: Liang told his staff, "Du Yu built a river bridge; we can do the same on the Wei."

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「水淺，不可為浮橋，汎長無恒，又不可施柱，恐難成立。」

translations.literal: All said: "The water is shallow—not fit for a floating bridge; the flood has no constancy, nor can pillars be set—We fear it will be hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Staff said a floating bridge was impossible—the river was too shallow and unstable.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「昔秦居咸陽，橫橋渡渭，以像閣道，此即以柱為橋。

translations.literal: Liang said: "Formerly Qin at Xianyang crossed the Wei with a horizontal bridge like a gallery road—this used pillars as bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "Qin at Xianyang bridged the Wei with pillars—that is our model.

sentences.zh: 今唯慮長柱不可得耳。」

translations.literal: Now We only worry long pillars cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Only long pillars might be hard to find.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，山水暴至，浮出長木數百根。

translations.literal: It happened heaven sent great rain and mountain floods suddenly arrived; several hundred long logs floated out.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains washed hundreds of long logs downriver.

sentences.zh: 藉此為用，橋遂成立，百姓利之，至今猶名崔公橋。

translations.literal: Using these the bridge was completed; the people profited; to this day it is still called Lord Cui's Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: With those logs the bridge was built; the people still call it Lord Cui's Bridge.

sentences.zh: 亮性公清，敏于斷決，所在並號稱職，三輔服其德政。

translations.literal: Liang's nature was fair and clean, sharp in judgment; everywhere he was called competent; the three auxiliaries submitted to his virtuous governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fair and decisive, he was praised everywhere; the capital region respected his governance.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉之，詔賜衣馬被褥。

translations.literal: Shizong praised this and ordered gifts of robes, horses, and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong rewarded him with robes, horses, and bedding.

sentences.zh: 後納其女為九嬪，徵為太常卿，攝吏部事。

translations.literal: Later his daughter was taken as one of the Nine Concubines; he was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acting for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter entered the palace; he was recalled as Director of Imperial Sacrifices, acting for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，出為撫軍將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he went out as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign he governed Ding as General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍左游擊將軍趙祖悅率眾偷據硤石。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Left Mobile Commander Zhao Zuyue led masses to steal and hold Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's commander Zhao Zuyue seized Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 詔亮假鎮南將軍，齊王蕭寶夤鎮東將軍，章武王融安南將軍，並使持節、都督諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Liang acting General Who Guards the South; Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin General Who Pacifies the East; Prince of Zhangwu Rong General Who Pacifies the South—all Bearers of the Staff, Commanders of All Military Affairs to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, Xiao Baoyin, and Prince Rong of Zhangwu were sent with staff authority against Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 靈太后勞遣亮等，賜戎服雜物。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling saw them off with labor and gave martial dress and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling saw them off with gifts and martial dress.

sentences.zh: 亮至硤石，祖悅出城逆戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Liang reached Xiashi; Zuyue came out to meet battle and was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiashi Liang routed Zuyue in open battle.

sentences.zh: 賊復於城外置二柵，欲拒官軍，亮焚擊破之，殺三千餘人。

translations.literal: The bandits again set two palisades outside the city to resist the government army; Liang burned and broke them, killing more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rebuilt outer palisades; Liang burned them and killed three thousand.

sentences.zh: 亮與李崇為水陸之期，日日進攻，而崇不至。

translations.literal: Liang and Li Chong set a joint land-and-water date and attacked daily, but Chong did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Li Chong agreed on joint land-and-water attacks, but Chong failed to come.

sentences.zh: 及李平至，崇乃進軍，共平硤石，語在平傳。

translations.literal: When Li Ping arrived, Chong then advanced; together they pacified Xiashi—the account is in Ping's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ping came, Chong advanced and Xiashi fell—the account is in Ping's biography.

sentences.zh: 靈太后賜亮璽書曰：「硤石既平，大勢全舉，淮堰孤危，自將奔遁。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent Liang a sealed letter: "Xiashi is pacified, the great momentum fully raised; the Huai dam stands isolated and perilous—they will themselves flee.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wrote, "Xiashi is taken; the Huai dam rebels will flee.

sentences.zh: 若仍敢遊魂，此當易以立計，擒翦蟻徒，應在旦夕。

translations.literal: If they still dare linger in spirit, this should be easy to plan; capturing and cutting the ant-like followers should be within dawn and dusk.
translations.idiomatic: If any remain, destroy them quickly.

sentences.zh: 將軍推轂所憑，親對其事，處分經略，宜共協齊，必令得掃盪之理，盡彼遺燼也。

translations.literal: General, you rely on the push-bar for support and face the affair personally; disposition and strategy should jointly align—must make sweeping reason complete and their remaining embers exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinate strategy to wipe out every remnant.

sentences.zh: 隨便守禦，及分渡掠截，扼其咽喉，防塞走路，期之全獲，無令漏逸。

translations.literal: Guard and defend as convenient, divide to cross, plunder, and intercept, choke their throat, block escape routes—expect full capture, allow no leak.
translations.idiomatic: Block escape routes and allow no fugitives.

sentences.zh: 若畏威降首者，自加蠲宥，以仁為本，任之雅算。

translations.literal: Those who fear authority and lower their heads—add exemption by yourself; take benevolence as root; trust to your elegant calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Spare those who surrender; act with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 一二往使別宣。」

translations.literal: One or two envoys will separately proclaim."
translations.idiomatic: Further orders will follow by envoy."

sentences.zh: 以功進號鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 李平部分諸軍，將水陸兼進，以討堰賊。

translations.literal: Li Ping divided the armies and would advance by land and water together to suppress the dam bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping planned a joint land-and-water assault on the dam rebels.

sentences.zh: 亮違平節度，以疾請還，隨表而發。

translations.literal: Liang violated Ping's command, pleaded illness to return, and set out following his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Liang defied Ping, pleaded illness, and returned without leave.

sentences.zh: 平表曰：「臣以蕭衍將湛僧珍、田道龍遊魂境內，猶未收跡，義之、神念尚住梁城，令都督崔亮權據下蔡，別將瓫生即往東岸，與亮接勢，以防橋道。

translations.literal: Ping memorialized: "Your servant, because Xiao Yan's generals Zhan Sengzhen and Tian Daolong linger within the borders still ungathered, Yizhi and Shennian still stay at Liang city—I ordered Commander Cui Liang provisionally to hold Xiaqi, Separate Commander Pansheng immediately to go to the eastern bank and join forces with Liang to guard the bridge route.
translations.idiomatic: Ping reported that Liang was assigned to hold Xiaqi and guard the bridge route while enemies remained active.

sentences.zh: 臣發引向堰，舍人曹道至，奉敕更有處分，而亮已輒還京。

translations.literal: Your servant advanced toward the dam; attendant Cao Dao arrived bearing an edict with further disposition—and Liang had already returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Ping advanced on the dam, Liang had already returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 按亮受付東南，推轂是託，誠應憂國忘家，致命為限。

translations.literal: According to Liang receiving charge of the southeast, the push-bar is entrusted—truly he should worry for the state and forget home, devote life as limit.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with the southeast, Liang should have forgotten home for the state.

sentences.zh: 而始屆汝陰，磐桓不進；

translations.literal: Yet at first reaching Runan he lingered and did not advance;
translations.idiomatic: At Runan he lingered without advancing;

sentences.zh: 暨到寇所，停淹八旬；

translations.literal: when he reached the bandits' place he stopped more than eighty days;
translations.idiomatic: at the enemy site he stalled eighty days;

sentences.zh: 所營土山攻道，並不克就。

translations.literal: earth mounds and assault paths he set up were not completed.
translations.idiomatic: his siege works never finished.

sentences.zh: 損費糧力，坐延歲序。

translations.literal: He wasted grain and strength and sat extending the year.
translations.idiomatic: He wasted supplies and time.

sentences.zh: 賴天威遠被，士卒憤激，東北騰上，垂至北門；

translations.literal: Relying on heaven's authority reaching far, soldiers were stirred; northeast they surged up, almost reaching the north gate;
translations.idiomatic: Only when soldiers surged northeast nearly to the north gate

sentences.zh: 而亮遲回，仍不肯上，臣逼以白刃，甫乃登陟。

translations.literal: yet Liang hesitated and still would not ascend; your servant forced with bare blades before he finally climbed.
translations.idiomatic: did Ping force Liang up the walls with drawn swords.

sentences.zh: 及平硤石，宜聽處分，方更肆其專恣，輕輒還歸。

translations.literal: When Xiashi was pacified he should have heard disposition; instead he again indulged his arbitrary will and lightly returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiashi fell Liang again returned on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 此而不糾，法將焉寄？

translations.literal: If this is not corrected, where will law reside?
translations.idiomatic: If this goes unpunished, law is dead.

sentences.zh: 按律『臨軍征討而故留不赴者死』，又云『軍還先歸者流』。

translations.literal: According to law, "On campaign facing the enemy and deliberately staying not going—death"; also, "After the army returns, going ahead first— exile."
translations.idiomatic: By law, deserting a campaign is death; returning ahead of the army is exile.

sentences.zh: 軍罷先還，尚有流坐，況亮被符令停，委棄而反，失乘勝之機，闕水陸之會？

translations.literal: After the army ends, going ahead still has exile punishment—how much more Liang, receiving a written order to stop, abandoning and returning, losing the moment of victory, missing the land-and-water rendezvous?
translations.idiomatic: Even routine early return earns exile—how much worse Liang's unauthorized withdrawal?

sentences.zh: 緣情據理，咎深『故留』。

translations.literal: Following feeling and according to reason, guilt is deeper than "deliberately staying."
translations.idiomatic: By reason his guilt exceeds deliberate desertion.

sentences.zh: 今處亮死，上議。」

translations.literal: Now punish Liang with death—superior deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Liang be sentenced to death."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「亮為臣不忠，去留自擅，既損威稜，違我經略。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "Liang as minister was disloyal; going and staying he acted on his own—already damaging authority and violating Our strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Liang was disloyal, coming and going at will, damaging Our strategy.

sentences.zh: 雖有小捷，豈免大咎。

translations.literal: Though he had small success, how can he escape great blame?
translations.idiomatic: Small success cannot erase great fault.

sentences.zh: 但吾攝御萬幾，庶茲惡殺，可特聽以功補過。」

translations.literal: But We hold ten thousand affairs; We wish thus to abhor killing—specially allow merit to offset fault."
translations.idiomatic: Yet We allow merit to offset fault.

sentences.zh: 及平至，亮與爭功於禁中，形於聲色。

translations.literal: When Ping arrived, Liang contended for merit in the palace, showing it in voice and face.
translations.idiomatic: When Ping arrived Liang quarreled over credit in the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋除殿中尚書，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director Within the Hall and transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Director Within the Hall and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時羽林新害張彝之後，靈太后令武官得依資入選。

translations.literal: At the time the guard corps had newly killed Zhang Yi; Empress Dowager Ling ordered military officers to enter selection by qualification.
translations.idiomatic: After the guard corps killed Zhang Yi, military officers were allowed into Personnel selection by seniority.

sentences.zh: 官員既少，應選者多，前尚書李韶循常擢人，百姓大為嗟怨。

translations.literal: Official posts were few while candidates were many; former Minister Li Shao promoted by routine—the people greatly lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were few and candidates many; Li Shao's routine promotions angered the people.

sentences.zh: 亮乃奏為格制，不問士之賢愚，專以停解日月為斷。

translations.literal: Liang then memorialized to establish a grid system, not asking whether gentlemen were worthy or foolish, taking only suspension and dismissal months and days as measure.
translations.idiomatic: Liang created a seniority grid ignoring merit, counting only months out of office.

sentences.zh: 雖復官須此人，停日後者終於不得；

translations.literal: Even if an office needed this man, the one with later stop date ultimately could not obtain it;
translations.idiomatic: Even when a post needed a capable man, seniority blocked him;

sentences.zh: 庸才下品，年月久者灼然先用。

translations.literal: mediocre talent of lower rank, with longer years, was clearly used first.
translations.idiomatic: mediocre men with longer service won first.

sentences.zh: 沉滯者皆稱其能。

translations.literal: Those sunk long all praised its capability.
translations.idiomatic: The long-serving praised the system.

sentences.zh: 亮外甥司空諮議劉景安書規亮曰：「殷周以鄉塾貢士，兩漢由州郡薦才，魏晉因循，又置中正。

translations.literal: Liang's nephew on his sister's side, Staff Advisor of the Ministry of Works Liu Jing'an, wrote advising Liang: "Yin and Zhou through village schools presented gentlemen; the two Han through provinces and commanderies recommended talent; Wei and Jin followed and also set Grand Assessors.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Liu Jing'an wrote, "Past dynasties selected talent by merit through schools, recommendations, and assessors.

sentences.zh: 諦觀在昔，莫不審舉，雖未盡美，足應十收六七。

translations.literal: Observing the past, none failed to examine and promote; though not fully perfect, enough to harvest six or seven from ten.
translations.idiomatic: Past systems, though imperfect, picked six or seven good men in ten.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷貢秀才，[5]止求其文，不取其理；

translations.literal: Yet the court presents Excellent Scholars, [5] seeking only their writing, not taking their principle;
translations.idiomatic: Today Excellent Scholars [5] are judged on prose, not substance;

sentences.zh: 察孝廉唯論章句，不及治道；

translations.literal: investigating Filial and Incorrupt only discusses chapter and phrase, not reaching governing the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Filial and Incorrupt candidates are judged on phrases, not governance;

sentences.zh: 立中正不考人才行業，空辨氏姓高下。

translations.literal: establishing Grand Assessors does not examine men's talent and conduct, emptyly distinguishing clan surname high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Assessors rank clans, not character.

sentences.zh: 至於取士之途不溥，沙汰之理未精。

translations.literal: As for the paths of taking gentlemen not being broad, the principle of sifting not being refined.
translations.idiomatic: The paths of selection are narrow and refinement lacking.

sentences.zh: 而舅屬當銓衡，宜須改張易調。

translations.literal: Yet uncle holds the balance of selection—should change and adjust.
translations.idiomatic: You hold Personnel—you should reform this.

sentences.zh: 如之何反為停年格以限之？

translations.literal: How turn instead to a stop-year grid to limit it?
translations.idiomatic: Why impose a seniority grid instead?

sentences.zh: 天下士子誰復修厲名行哉！」

translations.literal: Who among the empire's gentlemen will again cultivate and sharpen name and conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: Who will cultivate virtue under seniority rules?"

sentences.zh: 亮答書曰：「汝所言乃有深致。

translations.literal: Liang replied: "What you say has deep point.
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied, "You speak with depth.

sentences.zh: 吾乘時邀幸，得為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: I by the times received fortune and obtained being Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: I reached Personnel by fortune of the times.

sentences.zh: 當其壯也，尚不如人，況今朽老而居帝難之任。

translations.literal: In my prime I was still not equal to others—how much more now, decayed and old, occupying the emperor's difficult post.
translations.idiomatic: In my prime I was unequal to others; now old, I hold an impossible post.

sentences.zh: 常思同昇舉直，[6]以報明主之恩；

translations.literal: I always think to rise together and lift the straight, [6] to repay the enlightened lord's grace;
translations.idiomatic: I wished to promote the worthy [6] and repay the emperor's grace;

sentences.zh: 盡忠竭力，不為貽厥之累。

translations.literal: exhaust loyalty and strength, not be a burden passed to heirs.
translations.idiomatic: to serve loyally without burdening my heirs.

sentences.zh: 昨為此格，有由而然，今已為汝所怪，千載之後，誰知我哉？

translations.literal: Yesterday I made this grid because there was cause; now you already wonder at it—a thousand years hence, who will know me?
translations.idiomatic: I made the grid for cause; a thousand years hence who will judge me?

sentences.zh: 可靜念吾言，當為汝論之。

translations.literal: Quietly ponder my words; I will explain for you.
translations.idiomatic: Consider my explanation.

sentences.zh: 吾兼、正六為吏部郎，三為尚書，銓衡所宜，頗知之矣。

translations.literal: I was Concurrent and Regular Sixth Rank as Personnel Vice Director, three times Minister—I know fairly well what the balance should weigh.
translations.idiomatic: Three times in Personnel, I know the balance well.

sentences.zh: 但古今不同，時宜須異。

translations.literal: But ancient and modern differ; the times require difference.
translations.idiomatic: But times differ from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 昔有中正，品其才第，上之尚書，尚書據狀，量人授職，此乃與天下羣賢共爵人也。

translations.literal: Formerly there were Grand Assessors who graded talent ranks; upward to the Ministry—the Ministry according to the record measured men and granted posts: this was sharing rank with the empire's multitude of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Once assessors graded talent and the Ministry appointed by record—sharing power with the worthy.

sentences.zh: 吾謂當爾之時，無遺才，無濫舉矣，而汝猶云十收六七。

translations.literal: I hold that in such a time there was no lost talent, no reckless promotion—and you still say six or seven from ten.
translations.idiomatic: Even then you admit only six or seven in ten succeeded.

sentences.zh: 況今日之選專歸尚書，以一人之鑒照察天下。

translations.literal: How much more today's selection returns solely to the Ministry—one man's mirror illuminating the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Today one Ministry mirrors the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 劉毅所云：『一吏部、兩郎中而欲究竟人物，何異以管闚天，而求其博哉。』

translations.literal: What Liu Yi said: "One Ministry of Personnel, two vice directors—and you wish to exhaustively investigate persons: how is it different from viewing heaven through a tube and seeking its breadth?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi said one Personnel Ministry cannot survey all men, like viewing heaven through a tube.

sentences.zh: 今勳人甚多，又羽林入選，武夫崛起，不解書計，唯可彍弩前驅，指蹤捕噬而已。

translations.literal: Now merit-holders are very many; also guard corps enter selection; warriors rise, not understanding writing and reckoning—fit only to fill crossbows as vanguard, point and track capture and bite.
translations.idiomatic: Merit-holders and guard corps flood in—warriors who cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 忽令垂組乘軒，求其烹鮮之效，未曾操刀，而使專割。

translations.literal: Suddenly make them hang seals and ride carriages, seek their effect at cooking fresh meat—they never held a knife yet are made sole cutters.
translations.idiomatic: Making them officials is like giving knives to men who never cooked.

sentences.zh: 又武人至多，官員至少，不可周溥。

translations.literal: Also warriors are extremely many, official posts extremely few—not possible to reach everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors are many, posts few—no fair distribution.

sentences.zh: 設令十人共一官，猶無官可授，況一人望一官，何由可不怨哉？

translations.literal: Suppose ten men share one office—still no office to grant; how much more one man expecting one office—how can there be no resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Ten men per post would still leave men without posts—resentment is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 吾近面執，不宜使武人入選，請賜其爵，厚其祿。

translations.literal: I lately argued face to face: military men should not enter selection—please grant them noble rank, thick salary.
translations.idiomatic: I argued military men should take rank and salary, not civil posts.

sentences.zh: 既不見從，是以權立此格，限以停年耳。

translations.literal: When this was not followed, I therefore provisionally established this grid, limiting by stop-years only.
translations.idiomatic: Denied that, I imposed the seniority grid.

sentences.zh: 昔子產鑄刑書以救弊，叔向譏之以正法，何異汝以古禮難權宜哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Zichan cast penal writing to save decay; Shuxiang mocked him for orthodox law—how is that different from you using ancient rites to challenge expedient measure!
translations.idiomatic: Zichan cast penal codes to save decay; Shuxiang mocked him—as you mock my expedient.

sentences.zh: 仲尼云：德我者亦春秋，罪我者亦春秋。

translations.literal: Confucius said: those who praise me also do so in the Spring and Autumn; those who blame me also do so in the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said praise and blame alike belong to history.

sentences.zh: 吾之此指，其由是也。

translations.literal: My meaning here proceeds from that.
translations.idiomatic: My intent is the same.

sentences.zh: 但令當來君子，知吾意焉。」

translations.literal: Only let future gentlemen know my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let future gentlemen understand my intent."

sentences.zh: 後甄琛、元脩義、城陽王徽相繼為吏部尚書，利其便己，踵而行之。

translations.literal: Later Zhen Chen, Yuan Xiuyi, and Prince of Chengyang Hui in succession became Minister of Personnel; finding it convenient for themselves, they followed and enacted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhen Chen, Yuan Xiuyi, and Prince Hui of Chengyang kept the grid for their convenience.

sentences.zh: 自是賢愚同貫，涇渭無別，魏之失才，從亮始也。

translations.literal: From this worthy and foolish shared the same string; Jing and Wei had no distinction—Wei's loss of talent began with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: From then worthy and foolish were indistinguishable—Wei began losing talent with Liang.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中、太常卿，尋遷左光祿大夫、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon he was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant and Director of Imperial Sacrifices, then Left Grand Master and Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時劉騰擅權，亮託妻劉氏，傾身事之，故頻年之中名位隆赫，有識者譏之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Teng monopolized power; Liang relied on his wife's Liu clan and threw himself into serving Teng; therefore within several years name and rank blazed—men of judgment mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Teng held power Liang served him through his wife's kin and was mocked for rapid advancement.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 正光二年秋，疽發於背，肅宗遣舍人問疾，亮上表乞解僕射，送所負荷及印綬，詔不許。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Zhengguang a carbuncle broke out on his back; Suzong sent an attendant to inquire after his illness; Liang memorialized begging to resign the vice directorship, sending back his burden and seal and cord—the edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang 2 a back carbuncle broke out; he asked to resign vice director but was refused.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，詔給東園祕器、朝服一襲，賵物七百段、蠟三百斤。

translations.literal: Soon he died; an edict gave eastern-garden secret vessels, one set of court robes; funeral gifts seven hundred bolts and three hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died; the court sent funeral gifts of seven hundred bolts and three hundred jin of wax.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡曰貞烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Same Honors as the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ji; posthumous name Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with Same Honors as the Three Excellencies and Ji governor, titled Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 亮在雍州，讀杜預傳，見為八磨，嘉其有濟時用，遂教民為碾。

translations.literal: Liang in Yong Province read Du Yu's biography, saw the eight mills, praised their use for the age, and therefore taught the people milling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong Province Liang read Du Yu's biography, admired his mills, and taught the people milling.

sentences.zh: 及為僕射，奏於張方橋東堰穀水造水碾磨數十區，其利十倍，國用便之。

translations.literal: When he was Vice Director he memorialized east of Zhangfang Bridge to dam valley water and build several tens of water mills—profit tenfold; state use was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: As vice director he built dozens of water mills east of Zhangfang Bridge, tenfold profit to the state.

sentences.zh: 亮有三子，士安、士和、士泰，並強幹善於當世。

translations.literal: Liang had three sons: Shian, Shihe, and Shitai—all strong and capable in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's three sons Shian, Shihe, and Shitai were all capable men.

sentences.zh: 士安，歷尚書比部郎，卒於諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Shian passed through Gentleman of the Ministry's Comparison Bureau; he died as Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Shian served in the Comparison Bureau and died as Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General of the Left and Governor of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General of the Left and Guang governor.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟士和以子乾亨繼。

translations.literal: Without sons, younger brother Shihe's son Qianheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Without sons, nephew Qianheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乾亨，武定中，尚書都兵郎中。

translations.literal: Qianheng, in Wuding era, was Gentleman of the Ministry's Arms Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Qianheng in Wuding era served in the Arms Bureau.

sentences.zh: 士和，歷司空主簿、通直郎。

translations.literal: Shihe passed through Staff Controller of the Ministry of Works and Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shihe served as Staff Controller of Works and Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從亮征硤石，以軍勳拜冠軍將軍、中散大夫、西道行臺元脩義左丞，行涇州事。

translations.literal: Following Liang on the Xiashi campaign, by military merit he was appointed General Who Captures the Enemy, Grand Master of Palace Leisure, Western Circuit Mobile Office Yuan Xiuyi's Left Vice Director, acting Jing Governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the Xiashi campaign Shihe earned General Who Captures the Enemy and acted as Jing governor.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤之在關中，高選遼佐，以為督府長史。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin was in Guanzhong he highly selected distant aides and made him chief clerk of the command office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin in Guanzhong made him commandery chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時莫折念生遣使詐降，寶夤表士和兼度支尚書，為隴右行臺，令入秦撫慰，為念生所害。

translations.literal: At the time Moqi Niansheng sent envoys feigning surrender; Baoyin memorialized Shihe as Concurrent Minister of Revenue, Longyou Mobile Office, ordering entry into Qin to soothe—he was killed by Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to accept Moqi Niansheng's false surrender, Shihe was killed in Qin.

sentences.zh: 士泰，歷給事中、司空從事中郎、諫議大夫、司空司馬。

translations.literal: Shitai passed through Attendant Within, Staff Advisor of the Ministry of Works, Remonstrating Grand Master, and Staff Controller of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai served as Attendant Within, staff advisor, remonstrator, and Works staff controller.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，荊蠻侵斥，以士泰為龍驤將軍、征蠻別將，事平，以功賜爵五等男。

translations.literal: At the end of Suzong's reign Jing barbarians pressed; Shitai was made General of Dragon Cavalry and Separate Commander Against Barbarians; when the affair was pacified, by merit he was given the noble rank Fifth-Rank Baron.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Suzong's reign he suppressed Jing barbarians and was ennobled Fifth-Rank Baron.

sentences.zh: 建義初，遇害於河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he met harm at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyi he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈都督青兗二州諸軍事、鎮東將軍、青州刺史，諡曰文肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Commander of All Military Affairs in Qing and Yan Provinces, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qing; posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made commander of Qing and Yan, General Who Pacifies the East, and Qing governor, titled Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子肇師，襲爵。

translations.literal: Son Zhaoshi inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhaoshi inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 武定末，中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Chief Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuding he was Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 亮弟敬默，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Jingmo was Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Jingmo was Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 卒於征虜長史，贈南陽太守。

translations.literal: He died as Chief Clerk of the Campaign Against the Enemy; posthumously given Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Campaign Against the Enemy chief clerk; posthumously Nanyang administrator.

sentences.zh: 子思韶，從亮征硤石，以軍功賜爵武城子，為冀州別駕。

translations.literal: Son Sishao, following Liang on the Xiashi campaign, by military merit was given the noble rank Viscount of Wucheng and was Ji Province aide.
translations.idiomatic: Son Sishao earned Viscount of Wucheng on the Xiashi campaign and served as Ji aide.

sentences.zh: 敬默弟隱處，[7]青州州都。

translations.literal: Jingmo's younger brother Yinchu, [7] Qing Province provincial assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmo's brother Yinchu [7] was Qing provincial assessor.

sentences.zh: 亮以其賤出，殊不經紀，論者譏焉。

translations.literal: Liang because he was born of a low woman paid him no attention at all—discussants mocked this.
translations.idiomatic: Liang ignored Yinchu for low birth and was mocked.

sentences.zh: 亮從父弟光韶，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Liang's father's younger brother's son Guangshao was known for filial service to parents.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Guangshao was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 初除奉朝請。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 光韶與弟光伯雙生，操業相侔，特相友愛，遂經吏部尚書李沖，讓官於光伯，辭色懇至。

translations.literal: Guangshao and younger brother Guangbo were twins; conduct and learning matched each other; they especially loved each other; therefore through Minister of Personnel Li Chong he yielded office to Guangbo, words and color earnest to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Twin brothers Guangshao and Guangbo yielded offices to each other through Li Chong with earnest devotion.

sentences.zh: 沖為奏聞，高祖嘉而許之。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized and reported; Gaozu praised and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong reported it; Gaozu approved.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年，以光韶為司空行參軍，復請讓從叔和，曰：「臣誠微賤，未登讓品，屬逢唐朝，耻無讓德。」

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe, Guangshao was made Acting Army Controller of the Ministry of Works; again he requested yielding to younger cousin He, saying: "Your servant is truly lowly, not yet reaching the rank of yielding; meeting the Tang court, I am shamed to lack yielding virtue."
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 20 Guangshao again yielded office to cousin He, claiming unworthiness."

sentences.zh: 和亦謙退，辭而不當。

translations.literal: He also modestly declined, declining and not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: He too declined.

sentences.zh: 高祖善之，遂以和為廣陵王國常侍。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved; therefore He was made Regular Attendant of the Principality of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made He Regular Attendant of Guangling principality.

sentences.zh: 尋敕光韶兼祕書郎，掌校華林御書。

translations.literal: Soon Guangshao was ordered Concurrent Secretary Gentleman, managing collation of the Hualin imperial library.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao was ordered to collate the Hualin imperial library.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，除青州治中，後為司空騎兵參軍，又兼司徒戶曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was appointed Qing Province aide; later he was Army Cavalry Controller of the Ministry of Works, also Concurrent Household Bureau of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Suzong's reign he served Qing as aide, then Works cavalry controller and Education household bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為濟州輔國府司馬，刺史高植甚知之，政事多委訪焉。

translations.literal: He went out as Assistant to the Principality of Fuguo in Ji Province; Governor Gao Zhi knew him well and entrusted many administrative matters to consultation.
translations.idiomatic: As Ji assistant to Fuguo principality he was trusted by Governor Gao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 遷青州平東府長史，府解，敕知州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of Qing Province's Pacify-the-East Office; when the office dissolved, an order made him know provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Pacify-the-East chief clerk and then acting Qing governor.

sentences.zh: 光韶清直明斷，民吏畏愛之。

translations.literal: Guangshao was clean, straight, clear, and decisive; officials and people feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Clean and decisive, he was feared and loved by officials and people.

sentences.zh: 入為司空從事中郎，以母老解官歸養，賦詩展意，朝士屬和者數十人。

translations.literal: He entered as Staff Advisor of the Ministry of Works; because his mother was old he resigned office to return and nourish her, composing poetry to express intent—court gentlemen harmonizing numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to care for his aged mother; dozens of courtiers harmonized with his farewell poem.

sentences.zh: 久之，徵為司徒諮議，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: After long time he was summoned as Staff Advisor of the Ministry of Education; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Education staff advisor, he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 光韶性嚴毅，聲韻抗烈，與人平談，常若震厲。

translations.literal: Guangshao's nature was stern and resolute; voice and tone were resisting and sharp; in level talk with men it was often like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and sharp-voiced, his ordinary speech sounded like thunder.

sentences.zh: 至於兄弟議論，外聞謂為忿怒，然孔懷雍睦，人少逮之。

translations.literal: As for brothers' discussion, outsiders hearing thought it anger—yet inner brotherly affection was harmonious; few matched it.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers' debates sounded like rage yet their bond was deeply harmonious.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，河間邢杲率河北流民十餘萬眾，攻逼州郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang, Xing Gao of Hejian led more than one hundred thousand northern refugees, attacking and pressing provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaozhuang's reign Xing Gao led a hundred thousand refugees against the provinces.

sentences.zh: 刺史元儁憂不自安，州人乞光韶為長史以鎮之。

translations.literal: Governor Yuan Jun was anxious and not at ease; provincials begged Guangshao as chief clerk to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuan Jun asked Guangshao as chief clerk to stabilize the province.

sentences.zh: 時陽平路回寓居齊土，與杲潛相影響，引賊入郭。

translations.literal: At the time Yangping Lu Hui dwelt in Qi territory, secretly echoing Gao, leading bandits into the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui of Yangping secretly colluded with Gao and led rebels into the city.

sentences.zh: 光韶臨機處分，在難確然。

translations.literal: Guangshao at the moment disposed; in difficulty he was firm.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao acted decisively in the crisis.

sentences.zh: 賊退之後，刺史表光韶忠毅，朝廷嘉之，發使慰勞焉。

translations.literal: After the bandits retreated the governor memorialized Guangshao's loyalty and resoluteness; the court praised it and sent envoys to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fled the governor praised his loyalty and the court sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 尋為東道軍司。

translations.literal: Soon he was Eastern Circuit Army Controller.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Eastern Circuit Army Controller.

sentences.zh: 及元顥入洛，自河以南，莫不風靡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, south of the river none did not sway.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang the south bank collapsed.

sentences.zh: 而刺史、廣陵王欣集文武以議所從。

translations.literal: The governor Prince of Guangling Xin gathered civil and military to discuss where to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Prince Xin of Guangling gathered officials to choose sides.

sentences.zh: 欣曰：「北海、長樂俱是同堂兄弟，今宗祏不移，我欲受赦，諸君意各何如？」

translations.literal: Xin said: "Beihai and Changle are both same-hall brothers; now the ancestral temple does not move—I wish to accept amnesty; gentlemen, what does each think?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "Beihai and Changle are kin; I wish to accept amnesty—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 在坐之人莫不失色，光韶獨抗言曰：「元顥受制梁國，稱兵本朝，拔本塞源，以資讎敵，賊臣亂子，曠代少儔，何但大王家事所宜切齒，等荷朝眷，未敢仰從。」

translations.literal: Those seated all lost color; Guangshao alone spoke resisting: "Yuan Hao controlled by the Liang state, raised arms against this court, uprooting the root and blocking the source to aid the enemy—rebel minister and disorderly son, rare in any age; not only the great king's household affair should gnash teeth—all equally bear court favor and dare not follow upward."
translations.idiomatic: All paled; Guangshao alone refused: "Hao is a Liang puppet rebel—we who owe the court dare not submit."

sentences.zh: 長史崔景茂、前瀛州刺史張烈、前郢州刺史房叔祖、徵士張僧皓咸云：「軍司議是。」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Cui Jingmao, former Ying Governor Zhang Lie, former Ying Governor Fang Shuzu, and recluse Zhang Senghao all said: "The army controller's argument is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Staff agreed with Guangshao."

sentences.zh: 欣乃斬顥使。

translations.literal: Xin then beheaded Hao's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Xin beheaded Hao's envoy.

sentences.zh: 尋徵輔國將軍、廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as General Who Assists the State and Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as General Who Assists the State and Vice Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 未至，除太尉長史，加左將軍，俄遷廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Before arriving he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Ministry of War, additionally General of the Left; soon he was transferred to Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before arriving he became Ministry of War chief clerk and soon Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時祕書監祖瑩以贓罪被劾，光韶必欲致之重法。

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat Director Zu Ying was impeached for bribery crime; Guangshao insisted on bringing him to heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ying was impeached for bribery Guangshao demanded heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 太尉、陽城王徽、尚書令、臨淮王彧、吏部尚書李神儁、侍中李彧，並勢望當時，皆為瑩求寬。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Yangcheng Hui, Director of the Secretariat Prince of Linhuai Yu, Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun, and Attendant Li Yu—all momentum and repute of the time— all sought leniency for Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Hui and Yu, Li Shenjun, and Li Yu all pleaded for Zu Ying.

sentences.zh: 光韶正色曰：「朝賢執事，於舜之功未聞有一，如何反為罪人言乎！」

translations.literal: Guangshao with stern color said: "Court worthies holding office—of Shun's achievements not one is heard; how turn instead to speak for the guilty!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao said, "You great men have done nothing like Shun—why speak for a criminal?"

sentences.zh: 其執意不回如此。

translations.literal: His fixed intent not turning was like this.
translations.idiomatic: He would not bend.

sentences.zh: 永安末，擾亂之際，遂還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongtai amid turmoil he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongtai he returned home amid turmoil.

sentences.zh: 光韶博學強辯，尤好理論，至於人倫名教得失之間，搉而論之，不以一毫假物。

translations.literal: Guangshao was broadly learned, strong in debate, especially fond of theoretical discussion; as for human relations and name-teaching gain and loss, he weighed and discussed—never lending one hair to things.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and argumentative, he debated ethics without compromise.

sentences.zh: 家足於財，而性儉吝，衣馬弊瘦，食味粗薄。

translations.literal: The household was sufficient in wealth yet by nature he was sparing and grudging; clothes and horses were worn and thin, food taste coarse and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy yet miserly, he wore thin clothes and ate coarse food.

sentences.zh: 始光韶在都，同里人王蔓於夜遇盜，害其二子。

translations.literal: When Guangshao was in the capital, fellow townsman Wang Man at night met robbers who killed his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital townsman Wang Man lost two sons to robbers at night.

sentences.zh: 孝莊詔黃門高道穆令加檢捕，一坊之內，家別搜索。

translations.literal: Xiaozhuang ordered Yellow Gate Gao Daomu to add search and capture; within one ward every house was searched separately.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhuang ordered searches house by house in the ward.

sentences.zh: 至光韶宅，綾絹錢布，匱篋充積。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangshao's residence, silk, cash, and cloth filled chests and baskets.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao's house was found full of silk and cash.

sentences.zh: 議者譏其矯嗇。

translations.literal: Discussants mocked his pretended stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: Critics mocked his pretended poverty.

sentences.zh: 其家資產，皆光伯所營。

translations.literal: His household assets were all managed by Guangbo.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbo managed the family wealth.

sentences.zh: 光伯亡，悉焚其契。

translations.literal: When Guangbo died he burned all the contracts.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbo died he burned all debt contracts.

sentences.zh: 河間邢子才曾貸錢數萬，後送還之。

translations.literal: Hejian Xing Zicai once lent money in tens of thousands; later he sent it back.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai once lent tens of thousands; when repaid

sentences.zh: 光韶曰：「此亡弟相貸，僕不知也。」

translations.literal: Guangshao said: "This was my late younger brother's loan; your servant did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao said, "That was my dead brother's loan—I knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 竟不納。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the repayment.

sentences.zh: 刺史元弼前妻，是光韶之繼室兄女，而弼貪婪，多諸不法，光韶以親情，亟相非責，弼銜之。

translations.literal: Governor Yuan Bi's former wife was Guangshao's stepmother's brother's daughter; Bi was greedy with many unlawful acts; Guangshao by kinship repeatedly reproved him; Bi harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuan Bi, related by marriage, was greedy; Guangshao rebuked him and Bi resented it.

sentences.zh: 時耿翔反於州界，弼誣光韶子通與賊連結，囚其合家，考掠非理，而光韶與之辯爭，辭色不屈，會樊子鵠為東道大使，知其見枉，理出之。

translations.literal: At the time Geng Xiang rebelled in the province borders; Bi falsely charged Guangshao's son Tong of connecting with the bandits, imprisoned the whole family, tortured unreasonably; Guangshao argued with him, words and color not yielding; when Fan Zihu became Eastern Circuit grand envoy and knew he was wronged, he released them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Bi framed Guangshao's son for treason; Guangshao argued unbowed until Fan Zihu cleared them.

sentences.zh: 時人勸令詣樊陳謝，光韶曰：「羊舌大夫已有成事，何勞往也。」

translations.literal: Men of the time urged him to go to Fan and thank him; Guangshao said: "Yangshe the grandee already had a completed affair—why trouble to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Urged to thank Fan Zihu, Guangshao said, "Yangshe the grandee needed no thanks—why should I?"

sentences.zh: 子鵠亦歎尚之。

translations.literal: Zihu also sighed and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan admired him all the same.

sentences.zh: 後刺史侯淵代下疑懼，停軍益都，謀為不軌。

translations.literal: Later Governor Hou Yuan replaced him, suspicious and fearful, halted the army at Yidu, plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governor Hou Yuan halted at Yidu plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 令數百騎夜入南郭，劫光韶，以兵脅之，責以謀略。

translations.literal: He ordered several hundred horsemen to enter the southern outer city at night, seizing Guangshao, coercing him with soldiers, demanding strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Hou sent horsemen to seize Guangshao at night and demand strategy.

sentences.zh: 光韶曰：「凡起兵者，須有名義，使君今日舉動直是作賊耳。

translations.literal: Guangshao said: "All who raise armies must have a righteous name; lord today acts—straightforwardly this is being bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao said, "Armies need righteous cause—you are simply bandits.

sentences.zh: 父老知復何計？」

translations.literal: Elders and commoners know again what plan?"
translations.idiomatic: What counsel can elders offer rebels?"

sentences.zh: 淵雖恨之，敬而不敢害。

translations.literal: Yuan though resentful respected him and did not dare harm.
translations.idiomatic: Hou hated but feared to harm him.

sentences.zh: 尋除征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，不起。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Cord; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Made General Who Campaigns East, he declined.

sentences.zh: 光韶以世道屯邅，朝廷屢變，閉門却掃，吉凶斷絕。

translations.literal: Guangshao because the world's way was troubled and the court repeatedly changed, closed his door and swept his path; fortune and misfortune he cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Amid turmoil he shut his door and cut off social ties.

sentences.zh: 誡子孫曰：「吾自謂立身無慚古烈，但以祿命有限，無容希世取進。

translations.literal: He admonished sons and grandsons: "I consider myself standing without shame before ancient heroes—but because fortune's mandate is limited, I cannot hope to take the age by advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He told heirs, "I stand without shame before ancients, but fortune limits ambition.

sentences.zh: 在官以來，不冒一級，官雖不達，經為九卿。

translations.literal: In office I have never stolen one rank; though office did not reach high, I have passed through nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I never stole rank; though not highest, I served nine ministries.

sentences.zh: 且吾平生素業，足以遺汝，官閥亦何足言也。

translations.literal: And my lifelong plain work is enough to bequeath you—what need to speak of official pedigree?
translations.idiomatic: My plain life's work suffices for you—pedigree is nothing.

sentences.zh: 吾既運薄，便經三娶，而汝之兄弟各不同生，合葬非古，吾百年之後，不須合也。

translations.literal: I am already unlucky in fate and have passed through three marriages; yet your brothers were not born of the same mother—joint burial is not ancient; after my hundred years do not require joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: Three marriages, sons by different mothers—do not bury me with them; joint burial is unancient.

sentences.zh: 然贈諡之及，出自君恩，豈容子孫自求之也，勿須求贈。

translations.literal: Yet posthumous title and posthumous name come from the lord's grace—how can sons and grandsons seek it themselves? Do not seek posthumous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors come from the throne—do not seek them.

sentences.zh: 若違吾志，如有神靈，不享汝祀。

translations.literal: If you violate my will, if spirits exist, they will not enjoy your sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Break my will and spirits will reject your sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟自幼及老，衣服飲食未曾一片不同，至於兒女官婚榮利之事，未嘗不先以推弟。

translations.literal: My brothers from youth to old age—in clothes and food never one piece different; as for sons' and daughters' official marriage glory and profit, never not first pushing to younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: My brothers shared everything; I always favored younger brothers in marriage and office.

sentences.zh: 弟頃橫禍，權作松櫬，亦可為吾作松棺，使吾見之。」

translations.literal: Younger brother recently met sudden calamity; provisionally made pine coffin—it can also be made for me so I may see it."
translations.idiomatic: My brother's pine coffin may serve for me too."

sentences.zh: 卒年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，侍中賈思同申啟，稱述光韶，贈散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing, Attendant Jia Sitong submitted a memorial praising Guangshao; posthumously he was given Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaojing Jia Sitong praised him; posthumously he was made Regular Attendant and Qing governor.

sentences.zh: 光韶弟光伯，尚書郎、青州別駕。

translations.literal: Guangshao's younger brother Guangbo was Secretariat Gentleman and Qing Province aide.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Guangbo was Secretariat Gentleman and Qing aide.

sentences.zh: 後以族弟休臨州，遂申牒求解。

translations.literal: Later because a clansman Xiu governed the province he submitted a petition requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When clansman Xiu became governor he asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏：「按禮：始封之君不臣諸父昆弟，封君之子臣昆弟不臣諸父，封君之孫得盡臣。

translations.literal: The Ministry memorialized: "According to rites: the lord first enfeoffed does not treat uncles and brothers as subjects; the enfeoffed lord's sons treat brothers as subjects but not uncles; the enfeoffed lord's grandsons may fully treat them as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reported: "By rite a first enfeoffed lord does not treat kin as subjects; his grandsons may treat all kin as subjects.

sentences.zh: 計始封之君，即是世繼之祖，尚不得臣，況今之刺史，既非世繼，而得行臣吏之節，執笏稱名者乎？

translations.literal: Calculating the first enfeoffed lord, he is the successive heir's ancestor and still cannot be treated as subject—how much more today's governors, who are not successive heirs, yet may perform the minister-subject's rites, hold the tablet and speak the name?
translations.idiomatic: The founding enfeoffed ancestor is not a subject—how can mere governors, not heirs, hold tablets and speak names as subjects?

sentences.zh: 檢光伯請解，率禮不愆，請宜許遂，以明道教。」

translations.literal: Examining Guangbo's request for dismissal, leading rites without fault—please appropriately permit completion to clarify teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbo's dismissal request follows rite without fault—grant it to clarify doctrine."

sentences.zh: 靈太后令從之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋除北海太守，有司以其更滿，依例奏代。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Beihai; the office because his term was full by precedent memorialized replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Beihai administrator; when his term ended the office requested replacement.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔曰：「光伯自莅海沂，清風遠著，兼其兄光韶復能辭榮侍養，兄弟忠孝，宜有甄錄，可更申三年，以厲風化。」

translations.literal: Suzong issued an edict: "Guangbo since governing Hai and Yi has clean wind reaching far; moreover his elder brother Guangshao again can resign glory to nourish parents—brothers' loyalty and filial piety should be specially recorded; may again extend three years to encourage custom."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong extended Guangbo three years for clean rule and brotherly filial piety."

sentences.zh: 後歷太傅諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Later he passed through Grand Tutor Staff Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Grand Tutor staff advisor.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，崔祖螭、張僧皓起逆，攻東陽，旬日之間，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the time of the deposed emperor, Cui Zuchi and Zhang Senghao raised rebellion, attacking Dongyang; within ten days masses exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor Cui Zuchi and Zhang Senghao rebelled at Dongyang with a hundred thousand men in ten days.

sentences.zh: 刺史、東萊王貴平欲令光伯出城慰勞。

translations.literal: The governor Prince of Donglai Guiping wished to make Guangbo go out of the city to comfort and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Prince Guiping of Donglai wanted Guangbo to leave the city to soothe the rebels.

sentences.zh: 兄光韶曰：「城民陵縱，為日已久，人人恨之，其氣甚盛。

translations.literal: Elder brother Guangshao said: "City people have been insolent for many days; every man hates them; their momentum is very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao said, "The city people have long resented outsiders; their rage is immense.

sentences.zh: 古人有言『眾怒如水火焉』，以此觀之，今日非可慰諭止也。」

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying, "The multitude's anger is like water and fire"—viewing by this, today is not a time for comfort and persuasion to stop."
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said, mob rage is like water and fire—soothing words will not stop it today."

sentences.zh: 貴平強之，光韶曰：「使君受委一方，董攝萬里，而經略大事，不與國士圖之。

translations.literal: Guiping forced it; Guangshao said: "The lord receives charge of one region, overseeing ten thousand li, yet on great strategy you do not plot with the state's gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Guiping forced him; Guangshao said, "You rule a region yet plot with lackeys, not worthies.

sentences.zh: 所共腹心，皆趨走羣小。

translations.literal: Those shared as heart and belly are all rushing servile petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Your intimates are all flatterers.

sentences.zh: 既不能綏遏以杜其萌，又不能坐觀，待其衰挫。

translations.literal: You can neither soothe and restrain to stop the sprout, nor sit and watch waiting for their decline and setback.
translations.idiomatic: You neither stop the sprout nor wait for collapse.

sentences.zh: 蹙迫小弟，從為無名之行。

translations.literal: You press a younger brother into a nameless act.
translations.idiomatic: You push my brother into a pointless errand.

sentences.zh: 若單騎獨往，或見拘縶，若以眾臨之，勢必相拒敵，懸見無益也。」

translations.literal: If he goes alone on one horse, perhaps he will be detained; if you come with masses, inevitably you will mutually resist—the hanging view shows no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Alone he may be seized; with troops you will fight—either way it fails."

sentences.zh: 貴平逼之，不得已，光伯遂出城。

translations.literal: Guiping forced him; having no way out, Guangbo then went out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Forced at last, Guangbo went out.

sentences.zh: 數里，城民以光伯兄弟羣情所繫，慮人劫留，防衞者眾。

translations.literal: Several li out, city people because the Guangbo brothers were tied to the crowd's feeling, fearing men would seize and detain them—the guard escort was numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Miles out, guards feared the brothers would be seized and escorted them heavily.

sentences.zh: 外人疑其欲戰，未及曉諭，為飛矢所中，卒。

translations.literal: Outsiders suspected they wished to fight; before dawn explanation, he was hit by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders thought it was an attack; before he could explain, a stray arrow killed him.

sentences.zh: 贈征東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Campaigns East and Governor of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns East and Qing governor.

sentences.zh: 子滔，武定末，殷州別駕。

translations.literal: Son Tao, at the end of Wuding, was Yin Province aide.
translations.idiomatic: Son Tao late in Wuding was Yin Province aide.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李崇以風質英重，毅然秀立，任當將相，望高朝野，美矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Li Chong by wind and substance was heroic and heavy, firmly eminent and outstanding, fit for general and minister, repute high in court and countryside—beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Li Chong was heroically weighty, fit for general and minister, famed in court and field— admirable.

sentences.zh: 崔亮既明達後事，動有名迹，於斷年之選，失之逾遠，救弊未聞，終為國蠹，「無所苟而已」，其若是乎？

translations.literal: Cui Liang was clear on later affairs and moved with named traces; in selection of stop-years he missed by far, saving decay unheard—ending as state bane; "nothing done carelessly"—is it like this?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang was clear in office yet his seniority grid lost talent far and wide, ending as a state plague—is that "doing nothing carelessly"?

sentences.zh: 光韶居雅仗正，有國士之風矣。

translations.literal: Guangshao dwelt in elegance relying on rectitude—with the bearing of a state's gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao stood on rectitude with a true grandee's bearing.

translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

translations.idiomatic: Hold the frontier by virtue; civil authority proclaimed—Song reads "righteous men," Ming edition

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 1596〉

translations.literal: "Civil men" fails logically; "you thereof" fits, though Ming editors may have changed it.
translations.idiomatic: "Civil men" fails logically; "you thereof" fits, though Ming editors may have changed it.

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6983〉

translations.idiomatic: Song edition also has "turmoil"—left unchanged.

translations.idiomatic: Issue bright edicts—Ce fu

translations.idiomatic: 〈same volume page〉

translations.idiomatic: "Way" may read "again."

translations.literal: According to "way issue" is unintelligible—suspect "again" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Way issue" is unintelligible; "again" is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 為尚書郭祚所委 諸本「祚」作「秬」，北史卷四四崔亮傳作「祚」。

translations.literal: Entrusted by Minister Guo Zuo All editions "Zuo" read "Ju"; Northern History vol. 44 Cui Liang biography reads "Zuo."
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted by Guo Zuo—editions corrupt to "Ju"; Northern History has "Zuo."

sentences.zh: 按元恪即位後，郭祚即兼吏部尚書，後正除尚書，見卷六四本傳，別無「郭秬」其人為此官。

translations.literal: After Yuan Ke's accession Guo Zuo concurrently held Personnel Minister, later full Minister—see vol. 64 biography; no "Guo Ju" held this post.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Ke's accession Guo Zuo held Personnel—no "Guo Ju" existed.

sentences.zh: 「秬」字訛，今據改。

translations.idiomatic: "Ju" is corrupt—emended to "Zuo."

sentences.zh: 而朝廷貢秀才 諸本無「秀」字，冊府卷六三八

translations.literal: Yet the court presents Excellent Scholars All editions lack "Excellent"; Ce fu vol. 638
translations.idiomatic: Court presents Excellent Scholars—all editions omit "Excellent"; Ce fu vol. 638

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 7653〉

translations.idiomatic: has it.

sentences.zh: 按當時秀才試文，孝廉試經，這裏「貢秀才」和下「察孝廉」並舉，顯脫「秀」字，今據補。

translations.literal: At the time Excellent Scholars tested writing, Filial and Incorrupt tested classics—here "present Excellent Scholars" and below "investigate Filial and Incorrupt" are paired; clearly "Excellent" is lost—supplemented per evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent Scholars tested writing, Filial and Incorrupt classics—"Excellent" was lost and is restored.

sentences.zh: 常思同昇舉直 冊府卷八四九

translations.literal: Always think rise together lift straight Ce fu vol. 849
translations.idiomatic: Rise together lift straight—Ce fu vol. 849

sentences.zh: 「同昇」作「昇賢」。

translations.literal: "rise together" reads "promote worthy."
translations.idiomatic: "Rise together" reads "promote worthy."

sentences.zh: 按「同昇舉直」文義較晦，疑作「昇賢」是。

translations.literal: According to "rise together lift straight" meaning is obscure—suspect "promote worthy" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Rise together lift straight" is obscure; "promote worthy" fits.

sentences.zh: 敬默弟隱處 北史卷四四「隱處」作「敬遠」。

translations.literal: Jingmo's younger brother Yinchu Northern History vol. 44 "Yinchu" reads "Jingyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Jingmo's brother Yinchu—Northern History reads "Jingyuan."

sentences.zh: 按亮字敬儒，弟兄以「敬」字排行，疑作「敬遠」是。

translations.literal: According to Liang styled Jingru; brothers use "Jing" in naming—suspect "Jingyuan" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers share "Jing" in naming—"Jingyuan" may be correct.

sentences.zh: 也可能「隱處」作「隱居」解，上下有脫文。

translations.literal: Also possible "Yinchu" means "living in seclusion"—text above and below may have lost passages.
translations.idiomatic: Or "Yinchu" means "living in seclusion"—text may be defective.
